# gh-1444: [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

## Goal — iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth (v1)

One sentence: **the iOS agent stops burning steps on sandbox friction** — skill files resolve transparently, every swallowed network request becomes a visible error, secret presence is verifiable without leaking, and timeout/no-exit messages are honest.

Evidence base: a real iOS session (fa on iOS, glm-5.3-flash → glm-5.3, 2026-10-09, task "check fa craft and voxel, create issue via create-goal skill" — succeeded as #1441, but ~35 of ~70 steps were sandbox-fighting, and the owner aborted the run twice because it looked stuck). Record indexes below refer to that session export.

## Why this framing

- Not "make iOS faster" (untestable) — a list of six concrete, evidence-backed friction classes, each with a mechanism fix.
- Not "port git to WASI" — the goal is honest failure + the cheapest unblock (codeload allowlist), not a git client.
- Retracts nothing; complements gh-1430/gh-1433 (stream liveness / log fidelity, CLI-side) — this card is the **iOS sandbox + app** side.

## Prior art / lineage — what was already fixed, what this card adds

This is the **third round** of the same campaign; nothing here duplicates a shipped AC — evidence dates 2026-10-09, AFTER both prior cards closed.

- **#337** (closed 2026-09) — round 1: python.wasm TLS via the host bridge, `curl -d @file` JSON bodies, write↔bash fs seam, SIGPIPE, capabilities discoverability. **Shipped and working in the 2026-10-09 session**: python urllib rode the bridge, `curl --data @file` POSTed a 10 KB issue body (→ #1441), `/tmp` files persisted across calls. **What remains → this card**: those same paths now fail *intermittently and silently* — the bridge drops requests into 0-byte successes (C3), a python POST hit a TLS handshake error through the bridge with no surfaced detail (rec 107). The #337 mechanisms work; their failure modes are quiet. This card makes the failures loud.
- **#692** (closed 2026-09, PR #704) — round 2: iOS sandbox fitness — visible auth errors, sandbox-aware system prompt + tool floor, viewport, bounded app-state, no empty assistant answers. **Shipped**: platform prompt confirmed in app.log (`platform=SandboxPlatform.ios`, 2312-char commands section). **What remains → this card**: the "no empty answers" invariant landed at the *assistant-message* level but not the *tool-result* level — `read builtin://skills/...` returned an empty string with no error (C2, rec 29 vs 32); C4 (secret PRESENT/ABSENT) is the proactive complement to #692's reactive auth-error bubbles — an auth failure should be preventable, not just visible; C5 (timeout text) is a new find.
- **#1151** (closed) — built-in skills on every surface; the `.pointer` stub dirs on iOS are its artifact — C1 makes the pointer transparent instead of leaving it for the agent to discover.
- **#1440** (open) — skills discovery freshness: sibling of C1, different subject — #1440 is the *index* freshness (mid-session-added skill invisible), C1 is *path resolution* (fs path ⇄ builtin path). Both feed the same "a skill the host offers is reachable by the agent" contract; implement together.
- **#1393** (closed) — mobile parity shell + jsr testing: same campaign, no mechanical overlap with C1–C8.

## Architecture

Subject: the **agent-facing surface of the iOS sandbox** (`SandboxedExecutionEnv` + WASM shell + network bridge + virtual fs), not the apps/widgets it hosts.

```text
model ──tool──> bash/read (WASM shell) ──> bridge ──> iOS host network/fs
                     │                        │
                     └── today: silent empty/0-byte success ← FIX: loud errors
skills dir (.fah/skills/*/**.pointer) ──read──> today: FileError ← FIX: follow pointer
secrets (SecretsExecutionEnv) ──env──> today: silently empty ← FIX: PRESENT/ABSENT signal
```

Invariants: a tool result is either a real payload or an explicit error — never a silent empty success; secret VALUES never appear in any result, notice, or log; the fs view of skills is read-only.

## Capability surface (friction class ⇄ fix ⇄ evidence)

| # | Friction (what the agent hit) | Fix (subject of the verb) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `read .fah/skills/create-goal/SKILL.md` → FileError; dir holds only `SKILL.md.pointer` (`builtin://...`); agent spent 3 steps discovering `builtin://` URIs work | `read`/bash **cat of a skill path follows the `.pointer`** transparently (fs path and builtin path become equivalent for reads) | rec 16, 23, 26→29/32 |
| C2 | `read builtin://skills/...` returned **empty string, no error**; retry returned content | virtual-fs read of builtin resources never returns silent empty — empty payload on a non-empty resource = explicit error, retried once by the harness | rec 29 vs 32 |
| C3 | curl via bridge intermittently: 0 bytes, no `-w` marker, jq "prints nothing", labels POST swallowed; python urllib POST → TLS handshake error; ≥8 steps of blind retry-diagnosis | the **bridge surfaces transport failures into the command result** (stderr line `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset`, status marker, request id) and logs them to app.log; NO automatic retry of non-idempotent verbs | rec 50–67, 107, 114 |
| C4 | `$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN` empty on first authenticated call ("Requires authentication"), later worked — indistinguishable secret-absence vs swallowed request | **secret presence is verifiable**: session-start notice and/or `env` listing print `FA_GITHUB_TOKEN: PRESENT/ABSENT`; redaction removes values, never the variable's existence signal | rec 64→65 |
| C5 | `find / -maxdepth 4` killed at 30s default; result text said "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation … may be unavailable" + "timed out after unknown seconds" | **timeout results tell the truth**: "command timed out after 30s — partial output: <tail>", exit-code failures never labeled "uncaught exception"; iOS default timeout raised (60–120s) for fs-wide scans | rec 26; app log `timeout 0:00:30` 184× |
| C6 | `git clone` HTTPS fails ("smart HTTP failed"); codeload.github.com tarball → 0 bytes (redirect blocked); agent rebuilt the repo via API search + per-file raw fetches (~30 steps) | **codeload.github.com allowed by the bridge** (same trust family as raw.githubusercontent.com which works); documented host matrix in the iOS system-prompt section; (second tier) a repo-tree fetch helper | rec 57–62 |
| C7 | every non-zero exit logged as `_start error: FrbAnyhowException(Exited with i32 exit status 1)` (error level) — grep-misses pollute app.log triage | **app.log hygiene**: normal exit codes → debug level; error level reserved for harness faults | app log: 14× exit 1, 7× exit 2 |
| C8 | python3 prints `Could not find platform dependent libraries <exec_prefix>` on every run; one heredoc run lost stdout entirely | (second tier) **WASI python runtime**: set exec_prefix/PYTHONHOME or suppress the warning; regression-test heredoc stdin passthrough | rec 83–85, 115 |

Tiering: **core** = C1–C5, C7 (small, mechanical, unblock every future iOS task). **Second tier** = C6 (allowlist line is core-adjacent and cheap; the tree-helper is tier 2), C8. **Excluded** (rationale): full git client in the sandbox — raw/codeload + API covers the read-only workflows agents actually run; a in-app live "what is the agent doing" status row — owned by the gh-1430/gh-1433 liveness family, not this card; unauthenticated open proxying of arbitrary hosts — security boundary stays.

### Security (every fix above is an external-content or secret path)

Threat model: bridge errors and secret-presence signals are themselves attacker-observable channels; skill pointers are harness-authored but live in app-writable storage. Invariants: bridge error lines carry host+error class, never request headers or bodies; `PRESENT/ABSENT` leaks presence only, never values (byte-scan tests assert no secret material in results/notices/logs); pointer-following reads resolve ONLY `builtin://skills/...` URIs — any other poin…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1453
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1453
- **Title**: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1444` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 31

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \

# gh-1444: [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

## Goal — iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth (v1)

One sentence: **the iOS agent stops burning steps on sandbox friction** — skill files resolve transparently, every swallowed network request becomes a visible error, secret presence is verifiable without leaking, and timeout/no-exit messages are honest.

Evidence base: a real iOS session (fa on iOS, glm-5.3-flash → glm-5.3, 2026-10-09, task "check fa craft and voxel, create issue via create-goal skill" — succeeded as #1441, but ~35 of ~70 steps were sandbox-fighting, and the owner aborted the run twice because it looked stuck). Record indexes below refer to that session export.

## Why this framing

- Not "make iOS faster" (untestable) — a list of six concrete, evidence-backed friction classes, each with a mechanism fix.
- Not "port git to WASI" — the goal is honest failure + the cheapest unblock (codeload allowlist), not a git client.
- Retracts nothing; complements gh-1430/gh-1433 (stream liveness / log fidelity, CLI-side) — this card is the **iOS sandbox + app** side.

## Prior art / lineage — what was already fixed, what this card adds

This is the **third round** of the same campaign; nothing here duplicates a shipped AC — evidence dates 2026-10-09, AFTER both prior cards closed.

- **#337** (closed 2026-09) — round 1: python.wasm TLS via the host bridge, `curl -d @file` JSON bodies, write↔bash fs seam, SIGPIPE, capabilities discoverability. **Shipped and working in the 2026-10-09 session**: python urllib rode the bridge, `curl --data @file` POSTed a 10 KB issue body (→ #1441), `/tmp` files persisted across calls. **What remains → this card**: those same paths now fail *intermittently and silently* — the bridge drops requests into 0-byte successes (C3), a python POST hit a TLS handshake error through the bridge with no surfaced detail (rec 107). The #337 mechanisms work; their failure modes are quiet. This card makes the failures loud.
- **#692** (closed 2026-09, PR #704) — round 2: iOS sandbox fitness — visible auth errors, sandbox-aware system prompt + tool floor, viewport, bounded app-state, no empty assistant answers. **Shipped**: platform prompt confirmed in app.log (`platform=SandboxPlatform.ios`, 2312-char commands section). **What remains → this card**: the "no empty answers" invariant landed at the *assistant-message* level but not the *tool-result* level — `read builtin://skills/...` returned an empty string with no error (C2, rec 29 vs 32); C4 (secret PRESENT/ABSENT) is the proactive complement to #692's reactive auth-error bubbles — an auth failure should be preventable, not just visible; C5 (timeout text) is a new find.
- **#1151** (closed) — built-in skills on every surface; the `.pointer` stub dirs on iOS are its artifact — C1 makes the pointer transparent instead of leaving it for the agent to discover.
- **#1440** (open) — skills discovery freshness: sibling of C1, different subject — #1440 is the *index* freshness (mid-session-added skill invisible), C1 is *path resolution* (fs path ⇄ builtin path). Both feed the same "a skill the host offers is reachable by the agent" contract; implement together.
- **#1393** (closed) — mobile parity shell + jsr testing: same campaign, no mechanical overlap with C1–C8.

## Architecture

Subject: the **agent-facing surface of the iOS sandbox** (`SandboxedExecutionEnv` + WASM shell + network bridge + virtual fs), not the apps/widgets it hosts.

```text
model ──tool──> bash/read (WASM shell) ──> bridge ──> iOS host network/fs
                     │                        │
                     └── today: silent empty/0-byte success ← FIX: loud errors
skills dir (.fah/skills/*/**.pointer) ──read──> today: FileError ← FIX: follow pointer
secrets (SecretsExecutionEnv) ──env──> today: silently empty ← FIX: PRESENT/ABSENT signal
```

Invariants: a tool result is either a real payload or an explicit error — never a silent empty success; secret VALUES never appear in any result, notice, or log; the fs view of skills is read-only.

## Capability surface (friction class ⇄ fix ⇄ evidence)

| # | Friction (what the agent hit) | Fix (subject of the verb) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `read .fah/skills/create-goal/SKILL.md` → FileError; dir holds only `SKILL.md.pointer` (`builtin://...`); agent spent 3 steps discovering `builtin://` URIs work | `read`/bash **cat of a skill path follows the `.pointer`** transparently (fs path and builtin path become equivalent for reads) | rec 16, 23, 26→29/32 |
| C2 | `read builtin://skills/...` returned **empty string, no error**; retry returned content | virtual-fs read of builtin resources never returns silent empty — empty payload on a non-empty resource = explicit error, retried once by the harness | rec 29 vs 32 |
| C3 | curl via bridge intermittently: 0 bytes, no `-w` marker, jq "prints nothing", labels POST swallowed; python urllib POST → TLS handshake error; ≥8 steps of blind retry-diagnosis | the **bridge surfaces transport failures into the command result** (stderr line `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset`, status marker, request id) and logs them to app.log; NO automatic retry of non-idempotent verbs | rec 50–67, 107, 114 |
| C4 | `$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN` empty on first authenticated call ("Requires authentication"), later worked — indistinguishable secret-absence vs swallowed request | **secret presence is verifiable**: session-start notice and/or `env` listing print `FA_GITHUB_TOKEN: PRESENT/ABSENT`; redaction removes values, never the variable's existence signal | rec 64→65 |
| C5 | `find / -maxdepth 4` killed at 30s default; result text said "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation … may be unavailable" + "timed out after unknown seconds" | **timeout results tell the truth**: "command timed out after 30s — partial output: <tail>", exit-code failures never labeled "uncaught exception"; iOS default timeout raised (60–120s) for fs-wide scans | rec 26; app log `timeout 0:00:30` 184× |
| C6 | `git clone` HTTPS fails ("smart HTTP failed"); codeload.github.com tarball → 0 bytes (redirect blocked); agent rebuilt the repo via API search + per-file raw fetches (~30 steps) | **codeload.github.com allowed by the bridge** (same trust family as raw.githubusercontent.com which works); documented host matrix in the iOS system-prompt section; (second tier) a repo-tree fetch helper | rec 57–62 |
| C7 | every non-zero exit logged as `_start error: FrbAnyhowException(Exited with i32 exit status 1)` (error level) — grep-misses pollute app.log triage | **app.log hygiene**: normal exit codes → debug level; error level reserved for harness faults | app log: 14× exit 1, 7× exit 2 |
| C8 | python3 prints `Could not find platform dependent libraries <exec_prefix>` on every run; one heredoc run lost stdout entirely | (second tier) **WASI python runtime**: set exec_prefix/PYTHONHOME or suppress the warning; regression-test heredoc stdin passthrough | rec 83–85, 115 |

Tiering: **core** = C1–C5, C7 (small, mechanical, unblock every future iOS task). **Second tier** = C6 (allowlist line is core-adjacent and cheap; the tree-helper is tier 2), C8. **Excluded** (rationale): full git client in the sandbox — raw/codeload + API covers the read-only workflows agents actually run; a in-app live "what is the agent doing" status row — owned by the gh-1430/gh-1433 liveness family, not this card; unauthenticated open proxying of arbitrary hosts — security boundary stays.

### Security (every fix above is an external-content or secret path)

Threat model: bridge errors and secret-presence signals are themselves attacker-observable channels; skill pointers are harness-authored but live in app-writable storage. Invariants: bridge error lines carry host+error class, never request headers or bodies; `PRESENT/ABSENT` leaks presence only, never values (byte-scan tests assert no secret material in results/notices/logs); pointer-following reads resolve ONLY `builtin://skills/...` URIs — any other poin…

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T14:29:15Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# gh-1444: [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

## Goal — iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth (v1)

One sentence: **the iOS agent stops burning steps on sandbox friction** — skill files resolve transparently, every swallowed network request becomes a visible error, secret presence is verifiable without leaking, and timeout/no-exit messages are honest.

Evidence base: a real iOS session (fa on iOS, glm-5.3-flash → glm-5.3, 2026-10-09, task "check fa craft and voxel, create issue via create-goal skill" — succeeded as #1441, but ~35 of ~70 steps were sandbox-fighting, and the owner aborted the run twice because it looked stuck). Record indexes below refer to that session export.

## Why this framing

- Not "make iOS faster" (untestable) — a list of six concrete, evidence-backed friction classes, each with a mechanism fix.
- Not "port git to WASI" — the goal is honest failure + the cheapest unblock (codeload allowlist), not a git client.
- Retracts nothing; complements gh-1430/gh-1433 (stream liveness / log fidelity, CLI-side) — this card is the **iOS sandbox + app** side.

## Prior art / lineage — what was already fixed, what this card adds

This is the **third round** of the same campaign; nothing here duplicates a shipped AC — evidence dates 2026-10-09, AFTER both prior cards closed.

- **#337** (closed 2026-09) — round 1: python.wasm TLS via the host bridge, `curl -d @file` JSON bodies, write↔bash fs seam, SIGPIPE, capabilities discoverability. **Shipped and working in the 2026-10-09 session**: python urllib rode the bridge, `curl --data @file` POSTed a 10 KB issue body (→ #1441), `/tmp` files persisted across calls. **What remains → this card**: those same paths now fail *intermittently and silently* — the bridge drops requests into 0-byte successes (C3), a python POST hit a TLS handshake error through the bridge with no surfaced detail (rec 107). The #337 mechanisms work; their failure modes are quiet. This card makes the failures loud.
- **#692** (closed 2026-09, PR #704) — round 2: iOS sandbox fitness — visible auth errors, sandbox-aware system prompt + tool floor, viewport, bounded app-state, no empty assistant answers. **Shipped**: platform prompt confirmed in app.log (`platform=SandboxPlatform.ios`, 2312-char commands section). **What remains → this card**: the "no empty answers" invariant landed at the *assistant-message* level but not the *tool-result* level — `read builtin://skills/...` returned an empty string with no error (C2, rec 29 vs 32); C4 (secret PRESENT/ABSENT) is the proactive complement to #692's reactive auth-error bubbles — an auth failure should be preventable, not just visible; C5 (timeout text) is a new find.
- **#1151** (closed) — built-in skills on every surface; the `.pointer` stub dirs on iOS are its artifact — C1 makes the pointer transparent instead of leaving it for the agent to discover.
- **#1440** (open) — skills discovery freshness: sibling of C1, different subject — #1440 is the *index* freshness (mid-session-added skill invisible), C1 is *path resolution* (fs path ⇄ builtin path). Both feed the same "a skill the host offers is reachable by the agent" contract; implement together.
- **#1393** (closed) — mobile parity shell + jsr testing: same campaign, no mechanical overlap with C1–C8.

## Architecture

Subject: the **agent-facing surface of the iOS sandbox** (`SandboxedExecutionEnv` + WASM shell + network bridge + virtual fs), not the apps/widgets it hosts.

```text
model ──tool──> bash/read (WASM shell) ──> bridge ──> iOS host network/fs
                     │                        │
                     └── today: silent empty/0-byte success ← FIX: loud errors
skills dir (.fah/skills/*/**.pointer) ──read──> today: FileError ← FIX: follow pointer
secrets (SecretsExecutionEnv) ──env──> today: silently empty ← FIX: PRESENT/ABSENT signal
```

Invariants: a tool result is either a real payload or an explicit error — never a silent empty success; secret VALUES never appear in any result, notice, or log; the fs view of skills is read-only.

## Capability surface (friction class ⇄ fix ⇄ evidence)

| # | Friction (what the agent hit) | Fix (subject of the verb) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `read .fah/skills/create-goal/SKILL.md` → FileError; dir holds only `SKILL.md.pointer` (`builtin://...`); agent spent 3 steps discovering `builtin://` URIs work | `read`/bash **cat of a skill path follows the `.pointer`** transparently (fs path and builtin path become equivalent for reads) | rec 16, 23, 26→29/32 |
| C2 | `read builtin://skills/...` returned **empty string, no error**; retry returned content | virtual-fs read of builtin resources never returns silent empty — empty payload on a non-empty resource = explicit error, retried once by the harness | rec 29 vs 32 |
| C3 | curl via bridge intermittently: 0 bytes, no `-w` marker, jq "prints nothing", labels POST swallowed; python urllib POST → TLS handshake error; ≥8 steps of blind retry-diagnosis | the **bridge surfaces transport failures into the command result** (stderr line `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset`, status marker, request id) and logs them to app.log; NO automatic retry of non-idempotent verbs | rec 50–67, 107, 114 |
| C4 | `$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN` empty on first authenticated call ("Requires authentication"), later worked — indistinguishable secret-absence vs swallowed request | **secret presence is verifiable**: session-start notice and/or `env` listing print `FA_GITHUB_TOKEN: PRESENT/ABSENT`; redaction removes values, never the variable's existence signal | rec 64→65 |
| C5 | `find / -maxdepth 4` killed at 30s default; result text said "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation … may be unavailable" + "timed out after unknown seconds" | **timeout results tell the truth**: "command timed out after 30s — partial output: <tail>", exit-code failures never labeled "uncaught exception"; iOS default timeout raised (60–120s) for fs-wide scans | rec 26; app log `timeout 0:00:30` 184× |
| C6 | `git clone` HTTPS fails ("smart HTTP failed"); codeload.github.com tarball → 0 bytes (redirect blocked); agent rebuilt the repo via API search + per-file raw fetches (~30 steps) | **codeload.github.com allowed by the bridge** (same trust family as raw.githubusercontent.com which works); documented host matrix in the iOS system-prompt section; (second tier) a repo-tree fetch helper | rec 57–62 |
| C7 | every non-zero exit logged as `_start error: FrbAnyhowException(Exited with i32 exit status 1)` (error level) — grep-misses pollute app.log triage | **app.log hygiene**: normal exit codes → debug level; error level reserved for harness faults | app log: 14× exit 1, 7× exit 2 |
| C8 | python3 prints `Could not find platform dependent libraries <exec_prefix>` on every run; one heredoc run lost stdout entirely | (second tier) **WASI python runtime**: set exec_prefix/PYTHONHOME or suppress the warning; regression-test heredoc stdin passthrough | rec 83–85, 115 |

Tiering: **core** = C1–C5, C7 (small, mechanical, unblock every future iOS task). **Second tier** = C6 (allowlist line is core-adjacent and cheap; the tree-helper is tier 2), C8. **Excluded** (rationale): full git client in the sandbox — raw/codeload + API covers the read-only workflows agents actually run; a in-app live "what is the agent doing" status row — owned by the gh-1430/gh-1433 liveness family, not this card; unauthenticated open proxying of arbitrary hosts — security boundary stays.

### Security (every fix above is an external-content or secret path)

Threat model: bridge errors and secret-presence signals are themselves attacker-observable channels; skill pointers are harness-authored but live in app-writable storage. Invariants: bridge error lines carry host+error class, never request headers or bodies; `PRESENT/ABSENT` leaks presence only, never values (byte-scan tests assert no secret material in results/notices/logs); pointer-following reads resolve ONLY `builtin://skills/...` URIs — any other poin…

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. - **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# gh-1444: [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

## Goal — iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth (v1)

One sentence: **the iOS agent stops burning steps on sandbox friction** — skill files resolve transparently, every swallowed network request becomes a visible error, secret presence is verifiable without leaking, and timeout/no-exit messages are honest.

Evidence base: a real iOS session (fa on iOS, glm-5.3-flash → glm-5.3, 2026-10-09, task "check fa craft and voxel, create issue via create-goal skill" — succeeded as #1441, but ~35 of ~70 steps were sandbox-fighting, and the owner aborted the run twice because it looked stuck). Record indexes below refer to that session export.

## Why this framing

- Not "make iOS faster" (untestable) — a list of six concrete, evidence-backed friction classes, each with a mechanism fix.
- Not "port git to WASI" — the goal is honest failure + the cheapest unblock (codeload allowlist), not a git client.
- Retracts nothing; complements gh-1430/gh-1433 (stream liveness / log fidelity, CLI-side) — this card is the **iOS sandbox + app** side.

## Prior art / lineage — what was already fixed, what this card adds

This is the **third round** of the same campaign; nothing here duplicates a shipped AC — evidence dates 2026-10-09, AFTER both prior cards closed.

- **#337** (closed 2026-09) — round 1: python.wasm TLS via the host bridge, `curl -d @file` JSON bodies, write↔bash fs seam, SIGPIPE, capabilities discoverability. **Shipped and working in the 2026-10-09 session**: python urllib rode the bridge, `curl --data @file` POSTed a 10 KB issue body (→ #1441), `/tmp` files persisted across calls. **What remains → this card**: those same paths now fail *intermittently and silently* — the bridge drops requests into 0-byte successes (C3), a python POST hit a TLS handshake error through the bridge with no surfaced detail (rec 107). The #337 mechanisms work; their failure modes are quiet. This card makes the failures loud.
- **#692** (closed 2026-09, PR #704) — round 2: iOS sandbox fitness — visible auth errors, sandbox-aware system prompt + tool floor, viewport, bounded app-state, no empty assistant answers. **Shipped**: platform prompt confirmed in app.log (`platform=SandboxPlatform.ios`, 2312-char commands section). **What remains → this card**: the "no empty answers" invariant landed at the *assistant-message* level but not the *tool-result* level — `read builtin://skills/...` returned an empty string with no error (C2, rec 29 vs 32); C4 (secret PRESENT/ABSENT) is the proactive complement to #692's reactive auth-error bubbles — an auth failure should be preventable, not just visible; C5 (timeout text) is a new find.
- **#1151** (closed) — built-in skills on every surface; the `.pointer` stub dirs on iOS are its artifact — C1 makes the pointer transparent instead of leaving it for the agent to discover.
- **#1440** (open) — skills discovery freshness: sibling of C1, different subject — #1440 is the *index* freshness (mid-session-added skill invisible), C1 is *path resolution* (fs path ⇄ builtin path). Both feed the same "a skill the host offers is reachable by the agent" contract; implement together.
- **#1393** (closed) — mobile parity shell + jsr testing: same campaign, no mechanical overlap with C1–C8.

## Architecture

Subject: the **agent-facing surface of the iOS sandbox** (`SandboxedExecutionEnv` + WASM shell + network bridge + virtual fs), not the apps/widgets it hosts.

```text
model ──tool──> bash/read (WASM shell) ──> bridge ──> iOS host network/fs
                     │                        │
                     └── today: silent empty/0-byte success ← FIX: loud errors
skills dir (.fah/skills/*/**.pointer) ──read──> today: FileError ← FIX: follow pointer
secrets (SecretsExecutionEnv) ──env──> today: silently empty ← FIX: PRESENT/ABSENT signal
```

Invariants: a tool result is either a real payload or an explicit error — never a silent empty success; secret VALUES never appear in any result, notice, or log; the fs view of skills is read-only.

## Capability surface (friction class ⇄ fix ⇄ evidence)

| # | Friction (what the agent hit) | Fix (subject of the verb) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `read .fah/skills/create-goal/SKILL.md` → FileError; dir holds only `SKILL.md.pointer` (`builtin://...`); agent spent 3 steps discovering `builtin://` URIs work | `read`/bash **cat of a skill path follows the `.pointer`** transparently (fs path and builtin path become equivalent for reads) | rec 16, 23, 26→29/32 |
| C2 | `read builtin://skills/...` returned **empty string, no error**; retry returned content | virtual-fs read of builtin resources never returns silent empty — empty payload on a non-empty resource = explicit error, retried once by the harness | rec 29 vs 32 |
| C3 | curl via bridge intermittently: 0 bytes, no `-w` marker, jq "prints nothing", labels POST swallowed; python urllib POST → TLS handshake error; ≥8 steps of blind retry-diagnosis | the **bridge surfaces transport failures into the command result** (stderr line `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset`, status marker, request id) and logs them to app.log; NO automatic retry of non-idempotent verbs | rec 50–67, 107, 114 |
| C4 | `$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN` empty on first authenticated call ("Requires authentication"), later worked — indistinguishable secret-absence vs swallowed request | **secret presence is verifiable**: session-start notice and/or `env` listing print `FA_GITHUB_TOKEN: PRESENT/ABSENT`; redaction removes values, never the variable's existence signal | rec 64→65 |
| C5 | `find / -maxdepth 4` killed at 30s default; result text said "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation … may be unavailable" + "timed out after unknown seconds" | **timeout results tell the truth**: "command timed out after 30s — partial output: <tail>", exit-code failures never labeled "uncaught exception"; iOS default timeout raised (60–120s) for fs-wide scans | rec 26; app log `timeout 0:00:30` 184× |
| C6 | `git clone` HTTPS fails ("smart HTTP failed"); codeload.github.com tarball → 0 bytes (redirect blocked); agent rebuilt the repo via API search + per-file raw fetches (~30 steps) | **codeload.github.com allowed by the bridge** (same trust family as raw.githubusercontent.com which works); documented host matrix in the iOS system-prompt section; (second tier) a repo-tree fetch helper | rec 57–62 |
| C7 | every non-zero exit logged as `_start error: FrbAnyhowException(Exited with i32 exit status 1)` (error level) — grep-misses pollute app.log triage | **app.log hygiene**: normal exit codes → debug level; error level reserved for harness faults | app log: 14× exit 1, 7× exit 2 |
| C8 | python3 prints `Could not find platform dependent libraries <exec_prefix>` on every run; one heredoc run lost stdout entirely | (second tier) **WASI python runtime**: set exec_prefix/PYTHONHOME or suppress the warning; regression-test heredoc stdin passthrough | rec 83–85, 115 |

Tiering: **core** = C1–C5, C7 (small, mechanical, unblock every future iOS task). **Second tier** = C6 (allowlist line is core-adjacent and cheap; the tree-helper is tier 2), C8. **Excluded** (rationale): full git client in the sandbox — raw/codeload + API covers the read-only workflows agents actually run; a in-app live "what is the agent doing" status row — owned by the gh-1430/gh-1433 liveness family, not this card; unauthenticated open proxying of arbitrary hosts — security boundary stays.

### Security (every fix above is an external-content or secret path)

Threat model: bridge errors and secret-presence signals are themselves attacker-observable channels; skill pointers are harness-authored but live in app-writable storage. Invariants: bridge error lines carry host+error class, never request headers or bodies; `PRESENT/ABSENT` leaks presence only, never values (byte-scan tests assert no secret material in results/notices/logs); pointer-following reads resolve ONLY `builtin://skills/...` URIs — any other poin…

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T14:29:15Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# gh-1444: [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

## Goal — iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth (v1)

One sentence: **the iOS agent stops burning steps on sandbox friction** — skill files resolve transparently, every swallowed network request becomes a visible error, secret presence is verifiable without leaking, and timeout/no-exit messages are honest.

Evidence base: a real iOS session (fa on iOS, glm-5.3-flash → glm-5.3, 2026-10-09, task "check fa craft and voxel, create issue via create-goal skill" — succeeded as #1441, but ~35 of ~70 steps were sandbox-fighting, and the owner aborted the run twice because it looked stuck). Record indexes below refer to that session export.

## Why this framing

- Not "make iOS faster" (untestable) — a list of six concrete, evidence-backed friction classes, each with a mechanism fix.
- Not "port git to WASI" — the goal is honest failure + the cheapest unblock (codeload allowlist), not a git client.
- Retracts nothing; complements gh-1430/gh-1433 (stream liveness / log fidelity, CLI-side) — this card is the **iOS sandbox + app** side.

## Prior art / lineage — what was already fixed, what this card adds

This is the **third round** of the same campaign; nothing here duplicates a shipped AC — evidence dates 2026-10-09, AFTER both prior cards closed.

- **#337** (closed 2026-09) — round 1: python.wasm TLS via the host bridge, `curl -d @file` JSON bodies, write↔bash fs seam, SIGPIPE, capabilities discoverability. **Shipped and working in the 2026-10-09 session**: python urllib rode the bridge, `curl --data @file` POSTed a 10 KB issue body (→ #1441), `/tmp` files persisted across calls. **What remains → this card**: those same paths now fail *intermittently and silently* — the bridge drops requests into 0-byte successes (C3), a python POST hit a TLS handshake error through the bridge with no surfaced detail (rec 107). The #337 mechanisms work; their failure modes are quiet. This card makes the failures loud.
- **#692** (closed 2026-09, PR #704) — round 2: iOS sandbox fitness — visible auth errors, sandbox-aware system prompt + tool floor, viewport, bounded app-state, no empty assistant answers. **Shipped**: platform prompt confirmed in app.log (`platform=SandboxPlatform.ios`, 2312-char commands section). **What remains → this card**: the "no empty answers" invariant landed at the *assistant-message* level but not the *tool-result* level — `read builtin://skills/...` returned an empty string with no error (C2, rec 29 vs 32); C4 (secret PRESENT/ABSENT) is the proactive complement to #692's reactive auth-error bubbles — an auth failure should be preventable, not just visible; C5 (timeout text) is a new find.
- **#1151** (closed) — built-in skills on every surface; the `.pointer` stub dirs on iOS are its artifact — C1 makes the pointer transparent instead of leaving it for the agent to discover.
- **#1440** (open) — skills discovery freshness: sibling of C1, different subject — #1440 is the *index* freshness (mid-session-added skill invisible), C1 is *path resolution* (fs path ⇄ builtin path). Both feed the same "a skill the host offers is reachable by the agent" contract; implement together.
- **#1393** (closed) — mobile parity shell + jsr testing: same campaign, no mechanical overlap with C1–C8.

## Architecture

Subject: the **agent-facing surface of the iOS sandbox** (`SandboxedExecutionEnv` + WASM shell + network bridge + virtual fs), not the apps/widgets it hosts.

```text
model ──tool──> bash/read (WASM shell) ──> bridge ──> iOS host network/fs
                     │                        │
                     └── today: silent empty/0-byte success ← FIX: loud errors
skills dir (.fah/skills/*/**.pointer) ──read──> today: FileError ← FIX: follow pointer
secrets (SecretsExecutionEnv) ──env──> today: silently empty ← FIX: PRESENT/ABSENT signal
```

Invariants: a tool result is either a real payload or an explicit error — never a silent empty success; secret VALUES never appear in any result, notice, or log; the fs view of skills is read-only.

## Capability surface (friction class ⇄ fix ⇄ evidence)

| # | Friction (what the agent hit) | Fix (subject of the verb) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `read .fah/skills/create-goal/SKILL.md` → FileError; dir holds only `SKILL.md.pointer` (`builtin://...`); agent spent 3 steps discovering `builtin://` URIs work | `read`/bash **cat of a skill path follows the `.pointer`** transparently (fs path and builtin path become equivalent for reads) | rec 16, 23, 26→29/32 |
| C2 | `read builtin://skills/...` returned **empty string, no error**; retry returned content | virtual-fs read of builtin resources never returns silent empty — empty payload on a non-empty resource = explicit error, retried once by the harness | rec 29 vs 32 |
| C3 | curl via bridge intermittently: 0 bytes, no `-w` marker, jq "prints nothing", labels POST swallowed; python urllib POST → TLS handshake error; ≥8 steps of blind retry-diagnosis | the **bridge surfaces transport failures into the command result** (stderr line `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset`, status marker, request id) and logs them to app.log; NO automatic retry of non-idempotent verbs | rec 50–67, 107, 114 |
| C4 | `$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN` empty on first authenticated call ("Requires authentication"), later worked — indistinguishable secret-absence vs swallowed request | **secret presence is verifiable**: session-start notice and/or `env` listing print `FA_GITHUB_TOKEN: PRESENT/ABSENT`; redaction removes values, never the variable's existence signal | rec 64→65 |
| C5 | `find / -maxdepth 4` killed at 30s default; result text said "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation … may be unavailable" + "timed out after unknown seconds" | **timeout results tell the truth**: "command timed out after 30s — partial output: <tail>", exit-code failures never labeled "uncaught exception"; iOS default timeout raised (60–120s) for fs-wide scans | rec 26; app log `timeout 0:00:30` 184× |
| C6 | `git clone` HTTPS fails ("smart HTTP failed"); codeload.github.com tarball → 0 bytes (redirect blocked); agent rebuilt the repo via API search + per-file raw fetches (~30 steps) | **codeload.github.com allowed by the bridge** (same trust family as raw.githubusercontent.com which works); documented host matrix in the iOS system-prompt section; (second tier) a repo-tree fetch helper | rec 57–62 |
| C7 | every non-zero exit logged as `_start error: FrbAnyhowException(Exited with i32 exit status 1)` (error level) — grep-misses pollute app.log triage | **app.log hygiene**: normal exit codes → debug level; error level reserved for harness faults | app log: 14× exit 1, 7× exit 2 |
| C8 | python3 prints `Could not find platform dependent libraries <exec_prefix>` on every run; one heredoc run lost stdout entirely | (second tier) **WASI python runtime**: set exec_prefix/PYTHONHOME or suppress the warning; regression-test heredoc stdin passthrough | rec 83–85, 115 |

Tiering: **core** = C1–C5, C7 (small, mechanical, unblock every future iOS task). **Second tier** = C6 (allowlist line is core-adjacent and cheap; the tree-helper is tier 2), C8. **Excluded** (rationale): full git client in the sandbox — raw/codeload + API covers the read-only workflows agents actually run; a in-app live "what is the agent doing" status row — owned by the gh-1430/gh-1433 liveness family, not this card; unauthenticated open proxying of arbitrary hosts — security boundary stays.

### Security (every fix above is an external-content or secret path)

Threat model: bridge errors and secret-presence signals are themselves attacker-observable channels; skill pointers are harness-authored but live in app-writable storage. Invariants: bridge error lines carry host+error class, never request headers or bodies; `PRESENT/ABSENT` leaks presence only, never values (byte-scan tests assert no secret material in results/notices/logs); pointer-following reads resolve ONLY `builtin://skills/...` URIs — any other poin…

## Why this framing

- Not "make iOS faster" (untestable) — a list of six concrete, evidence-backed friction classes, each with a mechanism fix.
- Not "port git to WASI" — the goal is honest failure + the cheapest unblock (codeload allowlist), not a git client.

## Prior art / lineage — what was already fixed, what this card adds

This is the **third round** of the same campaign; nothing here duplicates a shipped AC — evidence dates 2026-10-09, AFTER both prior cards closed.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1453
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1453
- **Title**: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1444` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 31
- **Additions**: +2386
- **Deletions**: -147
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T14:04:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T14:29:15Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# gh-1444: [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

## Goal — iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth (v1)

One sentence: **the iOS agent stops burning steps on sandbox friction** — skill files resolve transparently, every swallowed network request becomes a visible error, secret presence is verifiable without leaking, and timeout/no-exit messages are honest.

Evidence base: a real iOS session (fa on iOS, glm-5.3-flash → glm-5.3, 2026-10-09, task "check fa craft and voxel, create issue via create-goal skill" — succeeded as #1441, but ~35 of ~70 steps were sandbox-fighting, and the owner aborted the run twice because it looked stuck). Record indexes below refer to that session export.

## Why this framing

- Not "make iOS faster" (untestable) — a list of six concrete, evidence-backed friction classes, each with a mechanism fix.
- Not "port git to WASI" — the goal is honest failure + the cheapest unblock (codeload allowlist), not a git client.
- Retracts nothing; complements gh-1430/gh-1433 (stream liveness / log fidelity, CLI-side) — this card is the **iOS sandbox + app** side.

## Prior art / lineage — what was already fixed, what this card adds

This is the **third round** of the same campaign; nothing here duplicates a shipped AC — evidence dates 2026-10-09, AFTER both prior cards closed.

- **#337** (closed 2026-09) — round 1: python.wasm TLS via the host bridge, `curl -d @file` JSON bodies, write↔bash fs seam, SIGPIPE, capabilities discoverability. **Shipped and working in the 2026-10-09 session**: python urllib rode the bridge, `curl --data @file` POSTed a 10 KB issue body (→ #1441), `/tmp` files persisted across calls. **What remains → this card**: those same paths now fail *intermittently and silently* — the bridge drops requests into 0-byte successes (C3), a python POST hit a TLS handshake error through the bridge with no surfaced detail (rec 107). The #337 mechanisms work; their failure modes are quiet. This card makes the failures loud.
- **#692** (closed 2026-09, PR #704) — round 2: iOS sandbox fitness — visible auth errors, sandbox-aware system prompt + tool floor, viewport, bounded app-state, no empty assistant answers. **Shipped**: platform prompt confirmed in app.log (`platform=SandboxPlatform.ios`, 2312-char commands section). **What remains → this card**: the "no empty answers" invariant landed at the *assistant-message* level but not the *tool-result* level — `read builtin://skills/...` returned an empty string with no error (C2, rec 29 vs 32); C4 (secret PRESENT/ABSENT) is the proactive complement to #692's reactive auth-error bubbles — an auth failure should be preventable, not just visible; C5 (timeout text) is a new find.
- **#1151** (closed) — built-in skills on every surface; the `.pointer` stub dirs on iOS are its artifact — C1 makes the pointer transparent instead of leaving it for the agent to discover.
- **#1440** (open) — skills discovery freshness: sibling of C1, different subject — #1440 is the *index* freshness (mid-session-added skill invisible), C1 is *path resolution* (fs path ⇄ builtin path). Both feed the same "a skill the host offers is reachable by the agent" contract; implement together.
- **#1393** (closed) — mobile parity shell + jsr testing: same campaign, no mechanical overlap with C1–C8.

## Architecture

Subject: the **agent-facing surface of the iOS sandbox** (`SandboxedExecutionEnv` + WASM shell + network bridge + virtual fs), not the apps/widgets it hosts.

```text
model ──tool──> bash/read (WASM shell) ──> bridge ──> iOS host network/fs
                     │                        │
                     └── today: silent empty/0-byte success ← FIX: loud errors
skills dir (.fah/skills/*/**.pointer) ──read──> today: FileError ← FIX: follow pointer
secrets (SecretsExecutionEnv) ──env──> today: silently empty ← FIX: PRESENT/ABSENT signal
```

Invariants: a tool result is either a real payload or an explicit error — never a silent empty success; secret VALUES never appear in any result, notice, or log; the fs view of skills is read-only.

## Capability surface (friction class ⇄ fix ⇄ evidence)

| # | Friction (what the agent hit) | Fix (subject of the verb) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `read .fah/skills/create-goal/SKILL.md` → FileError; dir holds only `SKILL.md.pointer` (`builtin://...`); agent spent 3 steps discovering `builtin://` URIs work | `read`/bash **cat of a skill path follows the `.pointer`** transparently (fs path and builtin path become equivalent for reads) | rec 16, 23, 26→29/32 |
| C2 | `read builtin://skills/...` returned **empty string, no error**; retry returned content | virtual-fs read of builtin resources never returns silent empty — empty payload on a non-empty resource = explicit error, retried once by the harness | rec 29 vs 32 |
| C3 | curl via bridge intermittently: 0 bytes, no `-w` marker, jq "prints nothing", labels POST swallowed; python urllib POST → TLS handshake error; ≥8 steps of blind retry-diagnosis | the **bridge surfaces transport failures into the command result** (stderr line `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset`, status marker, request id) and logs them to app.log; NO automatic retry of non-idempotent verbs | rec 50–67, 107, 114 |
| C4 | `$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN` empty on first authenticated call ("Requires authentication"), later worked — indistinguishable secret-absence vs swallowed request | **secret presence is verifiable**: session-start notice and/or `env` listing print `FA_GITHUB_TOKEN: PRESENT/ABSENT`; redaction removes values, never the variable's existence signal | rec 64→65 |
| C5 | `find / -maxdepth 4` killed at 30s default; result text said "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation … may be unavailable" + "timed out after unknown seconds" | **timeout results tell the truth**: "command timed out after 30s — partial output: <tail>", exit-code failures never labeled "uncaught exception"; iOS default timeout raised (60–120s) for fs-wide scans | rec 26; app log `timeout 0:00:30` 184× |
| C6 | `git clone` HTTPS fails ("smart HTTP failed"); codeload.github.com tarball → 0 bytes (redirect blocked); agent rebuilt the repo via API search + per-file raw fetches (~30 steps) | **codeload.github.com allowed by the bridge** (same trust family as raw.githubusercontent.com which works); documented host matrix in the iOS system-prompt section; (second tier) a repo-tree fetch helper | rec 57–62 |
| C7 | every non-zero exit logged as `_start error: FrbAnyhowException(Exited with i32 exit status 1)` (error level) — grep-misses pollute app.log triage | **app.log hygiene**: normal exit codes → debug level; error level reserved for harness faults | app log: 14× exit 1, 7× exit 2 |
| C8 | python3 prints `Could not find platform dependent libraries <exec_prefix>` on every run; one heredoc run lost stdout entirely | (second tier) **WASI python runtime**: set exec_prefix/PYTHONHOME or suppress the warning; regression-test heredoc stdin passthrough | rec 83–85, 115 |

Tiering: **core** = C1–C5, C7 (small, mechanical, unblock every future iOS task). **Second tier** = C6 (allowlist line is core-adjacent and cheap; the tree-helper is tier 2), C8. **Excluded** (rationale): full git client in the sandbox — raw/codeload + API covers the read-only workflows agents actually run; a in-app live "what is the agent doing" status row — owned by the gh-1430/gh-1433 liveness family, not this card; unauthenticated open proxying of arbitrary hosts — security boundary stays.

### Security (every fix above is an external-content or secret path)

Threat model: bridge errors and secret-presence signals are themselves attacker-observable channels; skill pointers are harness-authored but live in app-writable storage. Invariants: bridge error lines carry host+error class, never request headers or bodies; `PRESENT/ABSENT` leaks presence only, never values (byte-scan tests assert no secret material in results/notices/logs); pointer-following reads resolve ONLY `builtin://skills/...` URIs — any other poin…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
