- **Title**: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1444` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 31
- **Additions**: +2386
- **Deletions**: -147
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T14:04:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T14:29:15Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# gh-1444: [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

## Goal — iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth (v1)

One sentence: **the iOS agent stops burning steps on sandbox friction** — skill files resolve transparently, every swallowed network request becomes a visible error, secret presence is verifiable without leaking, and timeout/no-exit messages are honest.

Evidence base: a real iOS session (fa on iOS, glm-5.3-flash → glm-5.3, 2026-10-09, task "check fa craft and voxel, create issue via create-goal skill" — succeeded as #1441, but ~35 of ~70 steps were sandbox-fighting, and the owner aborted the run twice because it looked stuck). Record indexes below refer to that session export.

## Why this framing

- Not "make iOS faster" (untestable) — a list of six concrete, evidence-backed friction classes, each with a mechanism fix.
- Not "port git to WASI" — the goal is honest failure + the cheapest unblock (codeload allowlist), not a git client.
- Retracts nothing; complements gh-1430/gh-1433 (stream liveness / log fidelity, CLI-side) — this card is the **iOS sandbox + app** side.

## Prior art / lineage — what was already fixed, what this card adds

This is the **third round** of the same campaign; nothing here duplicates a shipped AC — evidence dates 2026-10-09, AFTER both prior cards closed.

- **#337** (closed 2026-09) — round 1: python.wasm TLS via the host bridge, `curl -d @file` JSON bodies, write↔bash fs seam, SIGPIPE, capabilities discoverability. **Shipped and working in the 2026-10-09 session**: python urllib rode the bridge, `curl --data @file` POSTed a 10 KB issue body (→ #1441), `/tmp` files persisted across calls. **What remains → this card**: those same paths now fail *intermittently and silently* — the bridge drops requests into 0-byte successes (C3), a python POST hit a TLS handshake error through the bridge with no surfaced detail (rec 107). The #337 mechanisms work; their failure modes are quiet. This card makes the failures loud.
- **#692** (closed 2026-09, PR #704) — round 2: iOS sandbox fitness — visible auth errors, sandbox-aware system prompt + tool floor, viewport, bounded app-state, no empty assistant answers. **Shipped**: platform prompt confirmed in app.log (`platform=SandboxPlatform.ios`, 2312-char commands section). **What remains → this card**: the "no empty answers" invariant landed at the *assistant-message* level but not the *tool-result* level — `read builtin://skills/...` returned an empty string with no error (C2, rec 29 vs 32); C4 (secret PRESENT/ABSENT) is the proactive complement to #692's reactive auth-error bubbles — an auth failure should be preventable, not just visible; C5 (timeout text) is a new find.
- **#1151** (closed) — built-in skills on every surface; the `.pointer` stub dirs on iOS are its artifact — C1 makes the pointer transparent instead of leaving it for the agent to discover.
- **#1440** (open) — skills discovery freshness: sibling of C1, different subject — #1440 is the *index* freshness (mid-session-added skill invisible), C1 is *path resolution* (fs path ⇄ builtin path). Both feed the same "a skill the host offers is reachable by the agent" contract; implement together.
- **#1393** (closed) — mobile parity shell + jsr testing: same campaign, no mechanical overlap with C1–C8.

## Architecture

Subject: the **agent-facing surface of the iOS sandbox** (`SandboxedExecutionEnv` + WASM shell + network bridge + virtual fs), not the apps/widgets it hosts.

```text
model ──tool──> bash/read (WASM shell) ──> bridge ──> iOS host network/fs
                     │                        │
                     └── today: silent empty/0-byte success ← FIX: loud errors
skills dir (.fah/skills/*/**.pointer) ──read──> today: FileError ← FIX: follow pointer
secrets (SecretsExecutionEnv) ──env──> today: silently empty ← FIX: PRESENT/ABSENT signal
```

Invariants: a tool result is either a real payload or an explicit error — never a silent empty success; secret VALUES never appear in any result, notice, or log; the fs view of skills is read-only.

## Capability surface (friction class ⇄ fix ⇄ evidence)

| # | Friction (what the agent hit) | Fix (subject of the verb) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `read .fah/skills/create-goal/SKILL.md` → FileError; dir holds only `SKILL.md.pointer` (`builtin://...`); agent spent 3 steps discovering `builtin://` URIs work | `read`/bash **cat of a skill path follows the `.pointer`** transparently (fs path and builtin path become equivalent for reads) | rec 16, 23, 26→29/32 |
| C2 | `read builtin://skills/...` returned **empty string, no error**; retry returned content | virtual-fs read of builtin resources never returns silent empty — empty payload on a non-empty resource = explicit error, retried once by the harness | rec 29 vs 32 |
| C3 | curl via bridge intermittently: 0 bytes, no `-w` marker, jq "prints nothing", labels POST swallowed; python urllib POST → TLS handshake error; ≥8 steps of blind retry-diagnosis | the **bridge surfaces transport failures into the command result** (stderr line `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset`, status marker, request id) and logs them to app.log; NO automatic retry of non-idempotent verbs | rec 50–67, 107, 114 |
| C4 | `$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN` empty on first authenticated call ("Requires authentication"), later worked — indistinguishable secret-absence vs swallowed request | **secret presence is verifiable**: session-start notice and/or `env` listing print `FA_GITHUB_TOKEN: PRESENT/ABSENT`; redaction removes values, never the variable's existence signal | rec 64→65 |
| C5 | `find / -maxdepth 4` killed at 30s default; result text said "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation … may be unavailable" + "timed out after unknown seconds" | **timeout results tell the truth**: "command timed out after 30s — partial output: <tail>", exit-code failures never labeled "uncaught exception"; iOS default timeout raised (60–120s) for fs-wide scans | rec 26; app log `timeout 0:00:30` 184× |

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the

# RATCHET (issue #433): the threshold is pinned at the CURRENT worst score
# measured by the SAME pipeline the CI gate uses — `flutter test --coverage`

# number must come from this pipeline, not the core's).
# Bootstrap (2026-09-15): 2450.0 — `JsAppEngine._faCall` (CC 49, 0% line
# coverage). Descent #1 (same day): the issue's three named offenders went
# under the next milestone line (CRAP ≤ 40 each) and the threshold followed

# `main`, CC 29 at 0% coverage). Descent #2 (issue #475): both beasts
# decomposed into route-table dispatch + per-family handlers with a 51-test
# golden suite, and the cluster's own 812/702/600/506 beasts went down with

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1453
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1453
- **Title**: gh-1444 [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1444` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 31
- **Additions**: +2386
- **Deletions**: -147
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T14:04:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T14:29:15Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

</details>

# gh-1444: [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

## Goal — iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth (v1)

One sentence: **the iOS agent stops burning steps on sandbox friction** — skill files resolve transparently, every swallowed network request becomes a visible error, secret presence is verifiable without leaking, and timeout/no-exit messages are honest.

Evidence base: a real iOS session (fa on iOS, glm-5.3-flash → glm-5.3, 2026-10-09, task "check fa craft and voxel, create issue via create-goal skill" — succeeded as #1441, but ~35 of ~70 steps were sandbox-fighting, and the owner aborted the run twice because it looked stuck). Record indexes below refer to that session export.

## Why this framing

- Not "make iOS faster" (untestable) — a list of six concrete, evidence-backed friction classes, each with a mechanism fix.
- Not "port git to WASI" — the goal is honest failure + the cheapest unblock (codeload allowlist), not a git client.
- Retracts nothing; complements gh-1430/gh-1433 (stream liveness / log fidelity, CLI-side) — this card is the **iOS sandbox + app** side.

## Prior art / lineage — what was already fixed, what this card adds

This is the **third round** of the same campaign; nothing here duplicates a shipped AC — evidence dates 2026-10-09, AFTER both prior cards closed.

- **#337** (closed 2026-09) — round 1: python.wasm TLS via the host bridge, `curl -d @file` JSON bodies, write↔bash fs seam, SIGPIPE, capabilities discoverability. **Shipped and working in the 2026-10-09 session**: python urllib rode the bridge, `curl --data @file` POSTed a 10 KB issue body (→ #1441), `/tmp` files persisted across calls. **What remains → this card**: those same paths now fail *intermittently and silently* — the bridge drops requests into 0-byte successes (C3), a python POST hit a TLS handshake error through the bridge with no surfaced detail (rec 107). The #337 mechanisms work; their failure modes are quiet. This card makes the failures loud.
- **#692** (closed 2026-09, PR #704) — round 2: iOS sandbox fitness — visible auth errors, sandbox-aware system prompt + tool floor, viewport, bounded app-state, no empty assistant answers. **Shipped**: platform prompt confirmed in app.log (`platform=SandboxPlatform.ios`, 2312-char commands section). **What remains → this card**: the "no empty answers" invariant landed at the *assistant-message* level but not the *tool-result* level — `read builtin://skills/...` returned an empty string with no error (C2, rec 29 vs 32); C4 (secret PRESENT/ABSENT) is the proactive complement to #692's reactive auth-error bubbles — an auth failure should be preventable, not just visible; C5 (timeout text) is a new find.
- **#1151** (closed) — built-in skills on every surface; the `.pointer` stub dirs on iOS are its artifact — C1 makes the pointer transparent instead of leaving it for the agent to discover.
- **#1440** (open) — skills discovery freshness: sibling of C1, different subject — #1440 is the *index* freshness (mid-session-added skill invisible), C1 is *path resolution* (fs path ⇄ builtin path). Both feed the same "a skill the host offers is reachable by the agent" contract; implement together.
- **#1393** (closed) — mobile parity shell + jsr testing: same campaign, no mechanical overlap with C1–C8.

## Architecture

Subject: the **agent-facing surface of the iOS sandbox** (`SandboxedExecutionEnv` + WASM shell + network bridge + virtual fs), not the apps/widgets it hosts.

```text
model ──tool──> bash/read (WASM shell) ──> bridge ──> iOS host network/fs
                     │                        │
                     └── today: silent empty/0-byte success ← FIX: loud errors
skills dir (.fah/skills/*/**.pointer) ──read──> today: FileError ← FIX: follow pointer
secrets (SecretsExecutionEnv) ──env──> today: silently empty ← FIX: PRESENT/ABSENT signal
```

Invariants: a tool result is either a real payload or an explicit error — never a silent empty success; secret VALUES never appear in any result, notice, or log; the fs view of skills is read-only.

## Capability surface (friction class ⇄ fix ⇄ evidence)

| # | Friction (what the agent hit) | Fix (subject of the verb) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `read .fah/skills/create-goal/SKILL.md` → FileError; dir holds only `SKILL.md.pointer` (`builtin://...`); agent spent 3 steps discovering `builtin://` URIs work | `read`/bash **cat of a skill path follows the `.pointer`** transparently (fs path and builtin path become equivalent for reads) | rec 16, 23, 26→29/32 |
| C2 | `read builtin://skills/...` returned **empty string, no error**; retry returned content | virtual-fs read of builtin resources never returns silent empty — empty payload on a non-empty resource = explicit error, retried once by the harness | rec 29 vs 32 |
| C3 | curl via bridge intermittently: 0 bytes, no `-w` marker, jq "prints nothing", labels POST swallowed; python urllib POST → TLS handshake error; ≥8 steps of blind retry-diagnosis | the **bridge surfaces transport failures into the command result** (stderr line `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset`, status marker, request id) and logs them to app.log; NO automatic retry of non-idempotent verbs | rec 50–67, 107, 114 |
| C4 | `$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN` empty on first authenticated call ("Requires authentication"), later worked — indistinguishable secret-absence vs swallowed request | **secret presence is verifiable**: session-start notice and/or `env` listing print `FA_GITHUB_TOKEN: PRESENT/ABSENT`; redaction removes values, never the variable's existence signal | rec 64→65 |
| C5 | `find / -maxdepth 4` killed at 30s default; result text said "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation … may be unavailable" + "timed out after unknown seconds" | **timeout results tell the truth**: "command timed out after 30s — partial output: <tail>", exit-code failures never labeled "uncaught exception"; iOS default timeout raised (60–120s) for fs-wide scans | rec 26; app log `timeout 0:00:30` 184× |
| C6 | `git clone` HTTPS fails ("smart HTTP failed"); codeload.github.com tarball → 0 bytes (redirect blocked); agent rebuilt the repo via API search + per-file raw fetches (~30 steps) | **codeload.github.com allowed by the bridge** (same trust family as raw.githubusercontent.com which works); documented host matrix in the iOS system-prompt section; (second tier) a repo-tree fetch helper | rec 57–62 |
| C7 | every non-zero exit logged as `_start error: FrbAnyhowException(Exited with i32 exit status 1)` (error level) — grep-misses pollute app.log triage | **app.log hygiene**: normal exit codes → debug level; error level reserved for harness faults | app log: 14× exit 1, 7× exit 2 |
| C8 | python3 prints `Could not find platform dependent libraries <exec_prefix>` on every run; one heredoc run lost stdout entirely | (second tier) **WASI python runtime**: set exec_prefix/PYTHONHOME or suppress the warning; regression-test heredoc stdin passthrough | rec 83–85, 115 |

Tiering: **core** = C1–C5, C7 (small, mechanical, unblock every future iOS task). **Second tier** = C6 (allowlist line is core-adjacent and cheap; the tree-helper is tier 2), C8. **Excluded** (rationale): full git client in the sandbox — raw/codeload + API covers the read-only workflows agents actually run; a in-app live "what is the agent doing" status row — owned by the gh-1430/gh-1433 liveness family, not this card; unauthenticated open proxying of arbitrary hosts — security boundary stays.

### Security (every fix above is an external-content or secret path)

Threat model: bridge errors and secret-presence signals are themselves attacker-observable channels; skill pointers are harness-authored but live in app-writable storage. Invariants: bridge error lines carry host+error class, never request headers or bodies; `PRESENT/ABSENT` leaks presence only, never values (byte-scan tests assert no secret material in results/notices/logs); pointer-following reads resolve ONLY `builtin://skills/...` URIs — any other poin…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the

- **State**: open

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]

  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

# gh-1444: [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

## Goal — iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth (v1)

One sentence: **the iOS agent stops burning steps on sandbox friction** — skill files resolve transparently, every swallowed network request becomes a visible error, secret presence is verifiable without leaking, and timeout/no-exit messages are honest.

Evidence base: a real iOS session (fa on iOS, glm-5.3-flash → glm-5.3, 2026-10-09, task "check fa craft and voxel, create issue via create-goal skill" — succeeded as #1441, but ~35 of ~70 steps were sandbox-fighting, and the owner aborted the run twice because it looked stuck). Record indexes below refer to that session export.

## Why this framing

- Not "make iOS faster" (untestable) — a list of six concrete, evidence-backed friction classes, each with a mechanism fix.
- Not "port git to WASI" — the goal is honest failure + the cheapest unblock (codeload allowlist), not a git client.
- Retracts nothing; complements gh-1430/gh-1433 (stream liveness / log fidelity, CLI-side) — this card is the **iOS sandbox + app** side.

## Prior art / lineage — what was already fixed, what this card adds

This is the **third round** of the same campaign; nothing here duplicates a shipped AC — evidence dates 2026-10-09, AFTER both prior cards closed.

- **#337** (closed 2026-09) — round 1: python.wasm TLS via the host bridge, `curl -d @file` JSON bodies, write↔bash fs seam, SIGPIPE, capabilities discoverability. **Shipped and working in the 2026-10-09 session**: python urllib rode the bridge, `curl --data @file` POSTed a 10 KB issue body (→ #1441), `/tmp` files persisted across calls. **What remains → this card**: those same paths now fail *intermittently and silently* — the bridge drops requests into 0-byte successes (C3), a python POST hit a TLS handshake error through the bridge with no surfaced detail (rec 107). The #337 mechanisms work; their failure modes are quiet. This card makes the failures loud.
- **#692** (closed 2026-09, PR #704) — round 2: iOS sandbox fitness — visible auth errors, sandbox-aware system prompt + tool floor, viewport, bounded app-state, no empty assistant answers. **Shipped**: platform prompt confirmed in app.log (`platform=SandboxPlatform.ios`, 2312-char commands section). **What remains → this card**: the "no empty answers" invariant landed at the *assistant-message* level but not the *tool-result* level — `read builtin://skills/...` returned an empty string with no error (C2, rec 29 vs 32); C4 (secret PRESENT/ABSENT) is the proactive complement to #692's reactive auth-error bubbles — an auth failure should be preventable, not just visible; C5 (timeout text) is a new find.
- **#1151** (closed) — built-in skills on every surface; the `.pointer` stub dirs on iOS are its artifact — C1 makes the pointer transparent instead of leaving it for the agent to discover.
- **#1440** (open) — skills discovery freshness: sibling of C1, different subject — #1440 is the *index* freshness (mid-session-added skill invisible), C1 is *path resolution* (fs path ⇄ builtin path). Both feed the same "a skill the host offers is reachable by the agent" contract; implement together.
- **#1393** (closed) — mobile parity shell + jsr testing: same campaign, no mechanical overlap with C1–C8.

## Architecture

Subject: the **agent-facing surface of the iOS sandbox** (`SandboxedExecutionEnv` + WASM shell + network bridge + virtual fs), not the apps/widgets it hosts.

```text
model ──tool──> bash/read (WASM shell) ──> bridge ──> iOS host network/fs
                     │                        │
                     └── today: silent empty/0-byte success ← FIX: loud errors
skills dir (.fah/skills/*/**.pointer) ──read──> today: FileError ← FIX: follow pointer
secrets (SecretsExecutionEnv) ──env──> today: silently empty ← FIX: PRESENT/ABSENT signal
```

Invariants: a tool result is either a real payload or an explicit error — never a silent empty success; secret VALUES never appear in any result, notice, or log; the fs view of skills is read-only.

## Capability surface (friction class ⇄ fix ⇄ evidence)

| # | Friction (what the agent hit) | Fix (subject of the verb) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `read .fah/skills/create-goal/SKILL.md` → FileError; dir holds only `SKILL.md.pointer` (`builtin://...`); agent spent 3 steps discovering `builtin://` URIs work | `read`/bash **cat of a skill path follows the `.pointer`** transparently (fs path and builtin path become equivalent for reads) | rec 16, 23, 26→29/32 |
| C2 | `read builtin://skills/...` returned **empty string, no error**; retry returned content | virtual-fs read of builtin resources never returns silent empty — empty payload on a non-empty resource = explicit error, retried once by the harness | rec 29 vs 32 |
| C3 | curl via bridge intermittently: 0 bytes, no `-w` marker, jq "prints nothing", labels POST swallowed; python urllib POST → TLS handshake error; ≥8 steps of blind retry-diagnosis | the **bridge surfaces transport failures into the command result** (stderr line `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset`, status marker, request id) and logs them to app.log; NO automatic retry of non-idempotent verbs | rec 50–67, 107, 114 |
| C4 | `$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN` empty on first authenticated call ("Requires authentication"), later worked — indistinguishable secret-absence vs swallowed request | **secret presence is verifiable**: session-start notice and/or `env` listing print `FA_GITHUB_TOKEN: PRESENT/ABSENT`; redaction removes values, never the variable's existence signal | rec 64→65 |
| C5 | `find / -maxdepth 4` killed at 30s default; result text said "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation … may be unavailable" + "timed out after unknown seconds" | **timeout results tell the truth**: "command timed out after 30s — partial output: <tail>", exit-code failures never labeled "uncaught exception"; iOS default timeout raised (60–120s) for fs-wide scans | rec 26; app log `timeout 0:00:30` 184× |
| C6 | `git clone` HTTPS fails ("smart HTTP failed"); codeload.github.com tarball → 0 bytes (redirect blocked); agent rebuilt the repo via API search + per-file raw fetches (~30 steps) | **codeload.github.com allowed by the bridge** (same trust family as raw.githubusercontent.com which works); documented host matrix in the iOS system-prompt section; (second tier) a repo-tree fetch helper | rec 57–62 |
| C7 | every non-zero exit logged as `_start error: FrbAnyhowException(Exited with i32 exit status 1)` (error level) — grep-misses pollute app.log triage | **app.log hygiene**: normal exit codes → debug level; error level reserved for harness faults | app log: 14× exit 1, 7× exit 2 |
| C8 | python3 prints `Could not find platform dependent libraries <exec_prefix>` on every run; one heredoc run lost stdout entirely | (second tier) **WASI python runtime**: set exec_prefix/PYTHONHOME or suppress the warning; regression-test heredoc stdin passthrough | rec 83–85, 115 |

### Security (every fix above is an external-content or secret path)

Threat model: bridge errors and secret-presence signals are themselves attacker-observable channels; skill pointers are harness-authored but live in app-writable storage. Invariants: bridge error lines carry host+error class, never request headers or bodies; `PRESENT/ABSENT` leaks presence only, never values (byte-scan tests assert no secret material in results/notices/logs); pointer-following reads resolve ONLY `builtin://skills/...` URIs — any other poin…

When the shell's `env` builtin renders `renderEnvListingWithSecretPresence(env)`, the roster var is hidden. Good. But what about `printenv FA_SECRET_VARS` or `echo $FA_SECRET_VARS`? The value would be visible — names only, so fine.
   - What about other processes seeing the roster? Fine, names only.

3. **`timeoutSecondsFromMessage` regex**: `RegExp(r'timeout:\s*(\d+):(\d{1,2}):(\d{1,2})')` — parses `0:00:30` = 30. For `0:00:00.500`, the match `(\d{1,2})` for the last group would match `00` and then `.500` is not matched, so seconds = 0 → rounds up to 1. OK.

4. **curl `-w` regression fix**: `_renderCurlWriteOut` now takes `url: request.url` — for redirect-following clients (`_httpClient.send` follows redirects internally for IOClient), `request.url` is the ORIGINAL url, not the effective URL. The PR description says "Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly." But `request.url` is the original request URL, not the effective one after redirects. Real curl reports the final URL. This is a minor semantic gap — the value is now non-empty (the original URL) but not the *effective* URL when redirects happened. Suggestion-level.

5. **Quota check on first chunk**: In the E7 test, they push a `big` chunk of `maxCurlResponseBytes + 1` bytes — 256 MiB + 1 bytes allocation in a test. That's a 256 MiB Uint8List in a unit test — heavy but works. Note `builder.add(chunk)` adds the full chunk BEFORE checking `builder.length > maxCurlResponseBytes` — so the builder can exceed the cap by up to one chunk size. Acceptable.

   Also, when quota is exceeded, the code `break`s out of the loop without cancelling `streamedResponse.stream` — the stream subscription remains (not cancelled), potentially leaving the connection hanging. Real code should call `streamedResponse.stream` cancel... Actually breaking out of `await for` DOES cancel the stream subscription. Yes — `await for` cancels the subscription on break. OK good.

6. **`bridgeHostOfAuthority`**: strips scheme, path, and `:443`/`:80` suffix. But `host.indexOf(':')` — if host ends with `:8080`, it stays. Fine. Edge: IPv6 authority `[::1]:443` — `host.indexOf(':')` would cut at the first colon inside the brackets, producing `[`. Edge case, unlikely in practice (the bridge authorities are github.com family). Suggestion-level at most.

7. **`_requestMethod`**: `latin1.decode(raw)` on the whole raw request — decodes potentially the entire body as latin1. For big bodies this creates a big string just to get the method. Minor perf. Also base64.decode(encoded) is already available in the caller — they decode the full raw request again just for the method. Minor.

8. **`parseCatArgs`**: `-` handling: `arg.startsWith('-') && arg != '-' && arg != ''`. What about a negative-looking filename like `-file`? GNU cat treats `-file` as an option cluster... it would error `invalid option -- 'f'`. Their short-option error: `arg.startsWith('--') ? arg : arg.substring(0, 2)` → for `-file`, substring(0,2) = `-f` → error message `invalid option -- 'f'`. GNU-like. OK.

   What about combined flags like `-nb`? GNU cat supports combined flags; this parser: `arg.substring(0, 2)` = `-n` → error `invalid option -- 'n'`? Wait: `short = arg.startsWith('--') ? arg : arg.substring(0, 2)` = `-n` then `short.replaceAll('-','')` = `n` → error `invalid option -- 'n'`. Hmm, GNU would accept `-nb`. So `cat -nb file` errors where GNU accepts. That's a real (minor) regression vs the coreutils.wasm applet which presumably handles combined flags. Actually does coreutils.wasm cat support `-nb`? Probably yes since it's busybox-like/GNU-ish. So the Dart seam cat is a behavioral subset: combined short flags unsupported. If a model runs `cat -nE file`... well `-E` isn't in the subset anyway. But `cat -nb` is plausible. When the seam is active (pointer in play), `cat -nb` would now fail with "invalid option" instead of working. Actually wait — `_catNeedsPointerSeam` returns false on parse error → falls to the applet path → applet handles it. So `cat -nb plainfile` works via applet; `cat -nb <pointer file>`... `_catNeedsPointerSeam` calls `parseCatArgs(args)` first — parse error → return false → applet path → applet reads through WASI → FileError on pointer path. Hmm, so `cat -nb .fah/skills/x/SKILL.md` (pointer) → applet → fails with not-found instead of following pointer. Edge case inconsistency, minor.

   Also `-` flag handling: `parseCatArgs(['-'])` → files: `['-']` (stdin). Good.

9. **`applyCatNumbering`**: GNU numbering for `-n` on blank lines numbers them too — yes it does. `padLeft(6)` matches GNU (6-width). OK. But what about `\r\n` line endings or a final line without newline: `applyCatNumbering('a\nb')` → lines `['a','b']`, output `1\ta\n2\tb\n` — adds a trailing newline that wasn't input. GNU cat -n adds newline after last line? Actually GNU `cat -n` on input without trailing newline: outputs `     1\ta\n     2\tb` WITHOUT trailing newline (it doesn't add one). Let me verify: `printf 'a\nb' | cat -n` gives "     1\ta\n     2\tb" without trailing newline. Yes — cat doesn't add a trailing newline that wasn't there. The Dart impl adds `\n` after every line including the last. Minor divergence — the test even asserts `contains('2\tb')` instead of exact equality, hinting they knew. Suggestion-level.

10. **`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`**: uses latin1 decode/encode round trip — binary-unsafe for non-latin1 bytes (bytes ≥ 0x80 map to U+0080..U+00FF and encode back identically — actually latin1 round-trips ALL byte values 0-255 exactly). Yes, latin1 round-trips bytes 0–255 losslessly. OK good. But the filter drops noise lines from BOTH captured stderr and the onStderr callback — a real python program printing those exact lines legitimately (e.g., `echo "Consider setting PYTHONHOME"` to stderr) would have its output suppressed. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Files Changed**: 31

- **Created**: 2026-10-09T14:04:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T14:29:15Z

## PR Description

Closes #1444
### What changed
Made the mobile sandbox fail loudly instead of silently (gh-1444): skill reads resolve `.pointer` files transparently, every swallowed network request renders a structured `[bridge]` error, secret presence is verifiable (`NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT`), and timeout results tell the truth.

- **AC1 (pointer reads):** `read .fah/skills/<n>/SKILL.md` follows the sibling `.pointer` to the compiled-in body via a new pure `skill_pointer.dart` resolver — wired into the `read` tool (all hosts), a conditional `cat` seam on the WASI shell, and the web `MemoryShell` file seam. Only `builtin://skills/…` targets resolve; a foreign/corrupt pointer is refused loudly (E1). `builtin://` URIs are accepted as direct read operands.
- **AC2 (no silent empty):** a builtin-resource read that would return an empty payload fails with an error naming the resource id (E5) instead of a silent success.
- **AC3 (bridge loudness):** `bridge_errors.dart` renders `[bridge] GET api.github.com: connection reset (rid c…)` lines — the python HTTP bridge and the curl builtin surface them in the tool result **and** app.log; the bridge makes exactly one attempt (no auto-retry of non-idempotent verbs).
- **AC4 (secret presence):** `SecretsExecutionEnv` injects a names-only roster (`FA_SECRET_VARS`); the sandbox `env` builtin renders `NAME: PRESENT/ABSENT` — values never render; `revokeSecret` keeps the name visible as ABSENT (E3).
- **AC5 (honest timeouts):** bash timeout results render the real cap (never "unknown seconds"), carry the captured partial output, and no longer wear the "uncaught exception" hint; mobile WASI default timeout raised 30s → 120s; killed stages keep a 64 KiB output tail.
- **AC6 (codeload):** the GitHub host matrix (api/raw/codeload/objects.githubusercontent.com + the `curl -L codeload…/tar.gz` recipe) is documented in the mobile host profile (≤1000 chars guard kept); redirect-following curl verified by unit test.
- **AC7 (log hygiene):** normal WASI exit codes log as `_start exited (status N)`, not `_start error:` — error lines in app.log mean harness faults again.
- **AC8 (python noise):** the `Could not find platform dependent libraries` warning is filtered from captured stderr (`WasiPythonNoiseFilter`).
- **E2/E7:** a mid-body connection reset delivers the partial payload with a `[bridge] … after N bytes (truncated)` line and exit 18; responses are capped at 256 MiB with a quota error naming both byte counts (exit 63).

### Key decisions
- Pointer resolution is one pure module (`lib/src/skills/skill_pointer.dart`) shared by the read tool and both mobile shells — one behavior everywhere, unit-testable without WASM.
- `cat` stays a coreutils.wasm applet (the gh-1274/#1335 host-cwd projection is pinned at the WASM stage boundary); the shell dispatches to a Dart cat **only** when a pointer is actually in play (`_catNeedsPointerSeam`: `builtin://` operand, or a missing file whose `.pointer` sibling resolves — an existing file always wins).
- The presence roster rides the exec env (names only) — no new wire, shells stay decorator-agnostic.
- Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/tools test/env test/secrets test/agent
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/bridge_loud_failures_test.dart \
  test/builtin_skill_pointer_test.dart test/sandbox_registry_test.dart \
  test/memory_shell_test.dart test/wasm_shell_builtins_test.dart \
  test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart test/sandbox_secret_presence_test.dart \
  test/sandbox_curl_data_test.dart test/wasm_shell_host_cwd_test.dart
```

**Known pre-existing failures in this runner (not from this branch):** golden pixel tests (proven: `origin/main` fails them identically — font rasterization drift), `wasm_sandbox_toolchain_test` (no desktop `libwasm_run_dart.so` provisioned), `providers_queue_writer_io_test` + 6 `test/integration` e2e tests (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var; all 6 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Simulator-only E2E legs (AC1 byte-identical on device, AC6 real codeload tarball, AC7 app.log spot-check) need an iOS simulator run.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[model] -->|read .fah/skills/n/SKILL.md| RT[read tool]
  RT --> SP[skill_pointer resolver]
  SP -->|builtin://skills target| EMB[compiled-in SKILL.md]
  SP -->|foreign target| ERR[loud refusal]
  M -->|bash cat / env| WS[WASI shell]
  WS -->|cat + pointer in play| SEAM[Dart cat seam]
  WS -->|plain cat| APP[coreutils.wasm applet]
  SEAM --> SP
  WS -->|python bridge / curl| BR[bridge_errors lines]
  BR --> TR[tool result stderr] & LOG[app.log bridge tag]
  SE[SecretsExecutionEnv roster] -->|FA_SECRET_VARS| WS
```

# gh-1444: [GOAL] iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth

## Description

## Goal — iOS sandbox ergonomics: skills resolve, networks fail loudly, secrets prove presence, timeouts tell the truth (v1)

One sentence: **the iOS agent stops burning steps on sandbox friction** — skill files resolve transparently, every swallowed network request becomes a visible error, secret presence is verifiable without leaking, and timeout/no-exit messages are honest.

Evidence base: a real iOS session (fa on iOS, glm-5.3-flash → glm-5.3, 2026-10-09, task "check fa craft and voxel, create issue via create-goal skill" — succeeded as #1441, but ~35 of ~70 steps were sandbox-fighting, and the owner aborted the run twice because it looked stuck). Record indexes below refer to that session export.

## Why this framing

- Not "make iOS faster" (untestable) — a list of six concrete, evidence-backed friction classes, each with a mechanism fix.
- Not "port git to WASI" — the goal is honest failure + the cheapest unblock (codeload allowlist), not a git client.
- Retracts nothing; complements gh-1430/gh-1433 (stream liveness / log fidelity, CLI-side) — this card is the **iOS sandbox + app** side.

## Prior art / lineage — what was already fixed, what this card adds

2. **Security review points**:
   - `FA_SECRET_VARS` roster: names-only, but is the roster itself ever leaking? The roster rides the exec env — that means the roster env var is passed to every exec'd process (real env). Fine — names only.
   - Secret values: `mergedExecEnv` merges `_secrets` — the values are still injected into the exec env. That's pre-existing behavior.
   - One issue: in `secret_presence.dart`, `renderEnvListingWithSecretPresence` — plain vars render as `NAME=value`. But what if a *rostered* secret name is set to a real value by per-call env? Then `secretPresenceLine` renders PRESENT. OK.
   - Potential leak: in the `env` rendering, non-rostered entries render `NAME=value` — that's classic env behavior.
   - Wait — there's a subtle issue: `SecretsExecutionEnv.exec` passes `FA_SECRET_VARS` roster to the delegate. The delegate env now includes `FA_SECRET_VARS=FA_GITHUB_TOKEN ...`. When the shell's `env` builtin renders `renderEnvListingWithSecretPresence(env)`, the roster var is hidden. Good. But what about `printenv FA_SECRET_VARS` or `echo $FA_SECRET_VARS`? The value would be visible — names only, so fine.
   - What about other processes seeing the roster? Fine, names only.

3. **`timeoutSecondsFromMessage` regex**: `RegExp(r'timeout:\s*(\d+):(\d{1,2}):(\d{1,2})')` — parses `0:00:30` = 30. For `0:00:00.500`, the match `(\d{1,2})` for the last group would match `00` and then `.500` is not matched, so seconds = 0 → rounds up to 1. OK.

4. **curl `-w` regression fix**: `_renderCurlWriteOut` now takes `url: request.url` — for redirect-following clients (`_httpClient.send` follows redirects internally for IOClient), `request.url` is the ORIGINAL url, not the effective URL. The PR description says "Fixed a self-introduced curl `-w` regression (`%{url_effective}` rendered empty after the loud-failure refactor) by passing the effective URL explicitly." But `request.url` is the original request URL, not the effective one after redirects. Real curl reports the final URL. This is a minor semantic gap — the value is now non-empty (the original URL) but not the *effective* URL when redirects happened. Suggestion-level.

5. **Quota check on first chunk**: In the E7 test, they push a `big` chunk of `maxCurlResponseBytes + 1` bytes — 256 MiB + 1 bytes allocation in a test. That's a 256 MiB Uint8List in a unit test — heavy but works. Note `builder.add(chunk)` adds the full chunk BEFORE checking `builder.length > maxCurlResponseBytes` — so the builder can exceed the cap by up to one chunk size. Acceptable.

   Also, when quota is exceeded, the code `break`s out of the loop without cancelling `streamedResponse.stream` — the stream subscription remains (not cancelled), potentially leaving the connection hanging. Real code should call `streamedResponse.stream` cancel... Actually breaking out of `await for` DOES cancel the stream subscription. Yes — `await for` cancels the subscription on break. OK good.

6. **`bridgeHostOfAuthority`**: strips scheme, path, and `:443`/`:80` suffix. But `host.indexOf(':')` — if host ends with `:8080`, it stays. Fine. Edge: IPv6 authority `[::1]:443` — `host.indexOf(':')` would cut at the first colon inside the brackets, producing `[`. Edge case, unlikely in practice (the bridge authorities are github.com family). Suggestion-level at most.

7. **`_requestMethod`**: `latin1.decode(raw)` on the whole raw request — decodes potentially the entire body as latin1. For big bodies this creates a big string just to get the method. Minor perf. Also base64.decode(encoded) is already available in the caller — they decode the full raw request again just for the method. Minor.

8. **`parseCatArgs`**: `-` handling: `arg.startsWith('-') && arg != '-' && arg != ''`. What about a negative-looking filename like `-file`? GNU cat treats `-file` as an option cluster... it would error `invalid option -- 'f'`.
