# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after

  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).

  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the

Double-read of every operand file — performance cost on large files (e.g. `cat big.bin` reads it twice: once as string via _readSandboxText (full decode!) and once via WASM). For binary files, `_readSandboxText` reads as string — memory heavy. This is a real performance regression on the plain-cat path (the common path). For a 100MB binary file in the sandbox, `cat` now reads+decodes 100MB as UTF-8 string, then the applet reads it again through WASI. That's a meaningful perf hit. Better: use an existence check (stat/exists) instead of a full read. Let me check what _readSandboxText does and whether an exists-check API is available. This is IMPORTANT-level (performance).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the

Double-read of every operand file — performance cost on large files (e.g. `cat big.bin` reads it twice: once as string via _readSandboxText (full decode!) and once via WASM). For binary files, `_readSandboxText` reads as string — memory heavy. This is a real performance regression on the plain-cat path (the common path). Now, an important issue with the mid-body truncation handling in curl: when `truncated == true` and `-o` is used — the partial bytes are written to the output file, exit 18. OK.

One subtle issue: on quota exceeded (`quotaExceeded`), the partial bytes are DISCARDED (returns _error without writing to the output file even if `-o` was passed). That's fine for a quota error.

Another: when `quotaExceeded`, the stream is broken out of — `await for` break cancels subscription. Good.

BUT — one issue: the truncated case doesn't include a newline between `stderrLines.join('\n')` etc. Actually the formatting: `'${stderrLines.join('\n')}${stderrLines.isEmpty ? '' : '\n'}'` — if stderrLines has 1 line, output = line + '\n'. OK. If empty, `''`. And non-silent: `statusLine` + lines + '\n'. OK.

Now the `-s` (silent) flag: in real curl, `-s` suppresses the progress meter and error messages, but `[bridge]` lines are deliberately kept even in silent mode (the AC3 requirement: failure must be visible). That's a deliberate deviation from curl semantics (silent mode suppresses errors). Worth noting — in silent mode, real curl would NOT print the error; this builtin prints the bridge line even when silent. That's the point of the ticket (loud failures), fine.

Now the `_ok(writeOut, stderr, 18)` for truncated case: exit code 18 = CURLE_PARTIAL_FILE. Good.

Now — `host = uri.host.isEmpty ? parsed.url! : uri.host`. If the URL has no host (e.g., a file path), `parsed.url!` includes full path — the failure line would then include the PATH, contradicting "never paths" invariant in the doc comment ("The lines carry host + error class only"). Minor: for URL 'not-a-url', host = whole URL string. But then the request would fail... actually `Uri.parse('not-a-url')` succeeds (relative URI), `_curlRequest` builds a request with a relative URI → `http.Request` would throw on send. The error line would contain `not-a-url` — that's the user's own operand, not a leak of headers. Minor nit, not a real secret leak. Actually wait — the invariant says "never request headers, bodies, or query strings". A URL with a query string: `uri.host` strips query. Only when `uri.host.isEmpty` does the full URL (with query!) render. E.g. `curl https:///path?token=x` — malformed. Edge case; suggestion-level.

Now the request-id counter is a static mutable — fine for correlation.

`_nextCurlRid` uses wall-clock microseconds + counter — unique enough.

The PR description claims "passing the effective URL explicitly" — this fixes the null case (`response.request?.url` was null in the streamed path), but it's the original URL, not effective-after-redirect. Now, an important issue with the mid-body truncation handling in curl: when `truncated == true` and `-o` is used — the partial bytes are written to the output file, exit 18. OK.

One subtle issue: on quota exceeded (`quotaExceeded`), the partial bytes are DISCARDED (returns _error without writing to the output file even if `-o` was passed). That's fine for a quota error.

Another: when `quotaExceeded`, the stream is broken out of — `await for` break cancels subscription. Good.

BUT — one issue: the truncated case doesn't include a newline between `stderrLines.join('\n')` etc. Actually the formatting: `'${stderrLines.join('\n')}${stderrLines.isEmpty ? '' : '\n'}'` — if stderrLines has 1 line, output = line + '\n'. OK. If empty, `''`. And non-silent: `statusLine` + lines + '\n'. OK.

Now the `-s` (silent) flag: in real curl, `-s` suppresses the progress meter and error messages, but `[bridge]` lines are deliberately kept even in silent mode (the AC3 requirement: failure must be visible). That's a deliberate deviation from curl semantics (silent mode suppresses errors). Worth noting — in silent mode, real curl would NOT print the error; this builtin prints the bridge line even when silent. That's the point of the ticket (loud failures), fine.

Now the `_ok(writeOut, stderr, 18)` for truncated case: exit code 18 = CURLE_PARTIAL_FILE. Good.

Now — `host = uri.host.isEmpty ? parsed.url! : uri.host`. If the URL has no host (e.g., a file path), `parsed.url!` includes full path — the failure line would then include the PATH, contradicting "never paths" invariant in the doc comment ("The lines carry host + error class only"). Minor: for URL 'not-a-url', host = whole URL string. But then the request would fail... actually `Uri.parse('not-a-url')` succeeds (relative URI), `_curlRequest` builds a request with a relative URI → `http.Request` would throw on send. The error line would contain `not-a-url` — that's the user's own operand, not a leak of headers. Minor nit, not a real secret leak. Actually wait — the invariant says "never request headers, bodies, or query strings". A URL with a query string: `uri.host` strips query. Only when `uri.host.isEmpty` does the full URL (with query!) render. E.g. `curl https:///path?token=x` — malformed. Edge case; suggestion-level.

Now the request-id counter is a static mutable — fine for correlation.

`_nextCurlRid` uses wall-clock microseconds + counter — unique enough.

Now `_renderCurlWriteOut(url: request.url)` — as noted, request.url is the ORIGINAL url, not the effective one after redirects (package:http IOClient follows redirects internally but `request.url` remains the original). The PR description claims "passing the effective URL explicitly" — this fixes the null case (`response.request?.url` was null in the streamed path), but it's the original URL, not effective-after-redirect. Real curl `%{url_effective}` shows the LAST url. Deviation: minor correctness nit (SUGGESTION). Actually wait — was the old code using `http.Response.fromStream` which had `response.request`? In old code, `response.request?.url.toString() ?? ''` — for a redirect-followed response, `response.request` in package:http is the original request too. So the behavior is unchanged vs old code except no longer empty. OK — so it's actually a faithful restoration. Fine.

Now — one REAL issue in the curl drain: the `stderrLines` in silent mode. `parsed.silent` → stderr contains ONLY the bridge lines. Good.

Another potential issue: `builder.length` is in bytes. Good.

Wait, there's something about `quotaExceeded` — the error message: `'curl: (63) response body exceeds the sandbox limit: received ${builder.length} bytes, cap is $maxCurlResponseBytes\n'`. In the test, they allocate a 256MiB+1 Uint8List — that's a heavyweight test (allocates 256 MiB). It might be slow/OOM in CI. Actually `Uint8List(SandboxBuiltins.maxCurlResponseBytes + 1)` — 256 MiB allocation in a widget test... Flutter test runner default has memory limits; 256MiB allocation usually OK but adds runtime. Hmm, it passed presumably... CI failed though. Can't confirm which test failed. Note it.

Wait — but how did the pre-existing builtins handle this? Other builtins like `_tacBuiltin` use `hostFile.readAsString()` too but only AFTER `existsSync` — same latent issue but pre-existing. The NEW part: `_catNeedsPointerSeam` introduces a FULL TEXT READ of every `cat` operand on EVERY cat command (mobile), including the plain-applet path. So:

1. **`cat <binary file>` on mobile** → `_readSandboxText` throws FormatException → unhandled exception out of `exec` → the bash tool sees an exception → "uncaught exception" style failure (ironic, given AC5). This is a REAL regression for binary cats. How common is cat-ing binary files in the sandbox? Models do `cat file.bin | base64` etc. Actually wait — would it throw? `File.readAsString` with default utf8 — malformed bytes throw FormatException? Let me double check Dart behavior: `File.readAsString(encoding: utf8)` → calls `readAsBytes` then `utf8.decode(bytes)` — wait actually it uses `encoding.decode(bytes)` where utf8.decode has allowMalformed: false → throws FormatException on invalid sequences. Hmm, actually in dart:io, `readAsString` wraps decode errors? Let me check the Dart SDK: `_File.readAsString` → `super.readAsString` in `_IoBase`... it decodes with `_decodeBytes` ... Actually `File.readAsString` documentation: "Throws a FileSystemException if the operation fails." and for decode errors — the decoded error is a `FormatException`? Hmm. In dart:io: 

```dart
Future<String> readAsString({Encoding encoding = utf8}) {
  return _withRetainedBackendFile... readAsBytes().then((bytes) => encoding.decode(bytes));
}
```

`encoding.decode` for utf8 with allowMalformed false throws FormatException. So yes — FormatException propagates.

Hmm wait, but is it `utf8.decode(bytes, allowMalformed: false)`? `Utf8Codec.decode(bytes, {bool? allowMalformed})` — default allowMalformed false → throws FormatException. Hmm, but actually in `encoding.decode` — `const Utf8Codec().decode` calls `_Utf8Decoder(allowMalformed: false).convert` → throws FormatException on malformed. Yes.

So `cat` of a non-UTF-8 file (e.g. a downloaded tarball, PNG, zip) on the mobile shell:
- BEFORE this PR: coreutils.wasm applet → binary-safe, works (outputs bytes).
- AFTER: `_catNeedsPointerSeam` full-reads as text → FormatException → **unhandled exception, exec fails**.

messages.preview: Confirmed the binary-`cat` regression risk. Let me check `ShellExecOptions` fields (the hand-rebuilt options in `SecretsExecutionEnv` must not drop any) and the read/bash tool files.

blocks.text:
Confirmed: `File.readAsString()` throws `FileSystemException` on non-UTF-8 bytes.

So the flow on the mobile (WasiSandboxShell):
- `cat <binary-file>` (e.g., a downloaded tarball, PNG) — pre-PR: coreutils.wasm applet, binary-safe. Post-PR: `_catNeedsPointerSeam` → `_readSandboxText(path)` → `file.readAsString()` → **throws FileSystemException** → escapes `_runPipeline`/`exec` uncaught.

And even without a throw, `cat big.txt` gets double-read.

Wait — one more check: `_catBuiltin`'s own path uses `_readSandboxTextFollowPointers` → same throw for binary operand in mixed invocation. And `_catNeedsPointerSeam` is invoked for EVERY cat first.

Actually hold on — does the exception really escape `exec`? `_runPipeline` calls `_runPipelineStage` without try/catch (only `finally`). `_runPipelineStage` → `_runCommand` → `_catNeedsPointerSeam` throws. So the exception propagates through `_runPipeline` (finally cleanup runs), through `runShellScript`, out of `exec`. The `Shell` interface returns `Result` — callers don't expect throws. The bash tool wraps tool execution with try/catch → renders "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation" (the very text AC5 removes for timeouts). So `cat image.png` on iOS now produces an uncaught-exception tool error. REGRESSION — BLOCKING? It's a correctness bug in the changed code (crash of a previously-working command class). Severity: 🚨 BLOCKING per "merge would cause a bug".

Hmm — but wait. Is `cat` even reachable with binary files on mobile? Yes — users/models cat PNGs, tarballs. And AC6's own recipe downloads a tarball — `cat` of it isn't needed, but `tar -xzf` reads it. Still, `cat binary` is legitimate.

Also note: even a UTF-8 text cat now double-reads (seam probe + applet). Perf: IMPORTANT.

Next, let me look at other changed regions: memory_shell/paths.dart current state, builtin_tools_read.dart, builtin_tools_bash.dart context (timeoutArg usage), shell_jobs, agent_loop. Then check the env builtin in wasm_shell (`_envBuiltin`) — uses renderEnvListingWithSecretPresence on mobile too (saw in diff). 

Also check: `FA_SECRET_VARS` value in `_envBuiltin` on mobile — the roster rides `options.env`? In wasm_shell `_envBuiltin` merges `{...env, ...assignments}` where env is the stage env (which includes FA_SECRET_VARS via exec env). renderEnvListingWithSecretPresence hides FA_SECRET_VARS. Good.

But — `printenv FA_SECRET_VARS` on mobile: coreutils printenv applet reads env → prints names. Fine (names only).

Security check — `redact`: does the roster leak SECRET NAMES in logs? Names are like FA_GITHUB_TOKEN — presence of names in app.log? The roster env var is passed to WASI stages; the env values are visible in `rec.configs.single.env` (test logs). Not secret values. OK per threat model ("PRESENT/ABSENT leaks presence only").

One more security angle: `secretPresenceLine` renders `NAME: PRESENT` when a non-empty value is in env. Suppose a user sets a PLAIN env var named e.g. `PATH` — not rostered — renders `PATH=/bin`. Fine.

Now — an important behavioral check for `renderEnvListingWithSecretPresence`: the OLD behavior of `env` on the web shell printed ALL vars including secret values?? Pre-PR: `names.map((n) => '$n=${env[n]}')` — wait, the SecretsExecutionEnv injects secret VALUES into the exec env. So pre-PR, `env` in the sandbox PRINTED SECRET VALUES?! Hmm — no wait. Which env does the shell's env builtin see? The stage env = the exec env (with injected secret values). So pre-PR `env` would print `FA_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_...`! That was the leak AC4 fixes... The ticket says C4: "$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN empty on first authenticated call" and "redaction removes values, never the variable's existence signal". Hmm, but there's a jobLogRedactor / redaction layer. Anyway — this PR FIXES that leak for mobile/web shells. Good.

BUT: what about `echo $FA_GITHUB_TOKEN`? Still prints the value (by design, bash needs it). And `printenv FA_GITHUB_TOKEN` on mobile — printenv is a coreutils applet reading the WASI env → prints the VALUE. So secret values remain obtainable via printenv — pre-existing (bash expansion too). Fine, documented design ($NAME must work).

Desktop LocalShell: `env` builtin = real /usr/bin/env → prints `FA_SECRET_VARS=...` AND the actual secret values (pre-existing behavior — LocalShell env prints real env). Not changed here. The desktop surface isn't patched to render PRESENT/ABSENT — cross-sandbox REG inconsistency (ticket test plan explicitly says REG must behave identically or degrade with explicit note). On desktop, `env` will print values as before AND the roster var (names). The PR adds `FA_SECRET_VARS` to desktop env listings via LocalShell — meaning on DESKTOP, `env` now shows `FA_SECRET_VARS=FA_GITHUB_TOKEN ...` — a NEW env var visible to every child process and in every env dump. Benign (names only), but it changes desktop "byte-identical" REG goldens? The ticket non-goal says "No change to desktop CLI behavior beyond shared pure modules (guarded by REG goldens)". But SecretsExecutionEnv is shared — desktop CLI exec envs NOW carry FA_SECRET_VARS. That IS a desktop behavior change (env dumps in desktop bash now include the roster var; any test asserting exact env maps broke — they updated test/secrets/secrets_test.dart accordingly, which is core, so CI test-core should catch others... they did update). The REG golden claim "CLI/desktop unaffected paths byte-identical" is not quite true for env listings on desktop. Minor documentation/consistency gap. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? I'd say SUGGESTION-level note, since no values leak.

Wait, actually there IS a subtle leak-adjacent behavior: `SecretsExecutionEnv.mergedExecEnv` — when `_secrets` is empty AND `_knownNames` non-empty (e.g. app registered names but no grants): `return {..._secrets(empty), ...?options?.env, secretPresenceEnvVar: names.join(' ')}` — returns a NON-NULL env even when options?.env was null. Then `exec(command, options: _optionsWithMergedEnv(options))` — options with env={roster}. The delegate gets options with a non-null env. LocalShell merges options.env OVER Platform.environment — fine.

Now `_optionsWithMergedEnv` rebuilds ShellExecOptions by hand — drops any field not listed. Let me check ShellExecOptions fields to confirm stdinData/liveStdin coverage and look for copyWith.

Confirmed: `File.readAsString()` throws `FileSystemException` on non-UTF-8 bytes.

So the flow on the mobile (WasiSandboxShell):
- `cat <binary-file>` (e.g., a downloaded tarball, PNG) — pre-PR: coreutils.wasm applet, binary-safe. Post-PR: `_catNeedsPointerSeam` → `_readSandboxText(path)` → `file.readAsString()` → **throws FileSystemException** → escapes `_runPipeline`/`exec` uncaught.

And even without a throw, `cat big.txt` gets double-read.

Wait — one more check: `_catBuiltin`'s own path uses `_readSandboxTextFollowPointers` → same throw for binary operand in mixed invocation. And `_catNeedsPointerSeam` is invoked for EVERY cat first.

Actually hold on — does the exception really escape `exec`? `_runPipeline` calls `_runPipelineStage` without try/catch (only `finally`). `_runPipelineStage` → `_runCommand` → `_catNeedsPointerSeam` throws. So the exception propagates through `_runPipeline` (finally cleanup runs), through `runShellScript`, out of `exec`. The `Shell` interface returns `Result` — callers don't expect throws. The bash tool wraps tool execution with try/catch → renders "uncaught exception inside the harness tool implementation" (the very text AC5 removes for timeouts). So `cat image.png` on iOS now produces an uncaught-exception tool error. REGRESSION — BLOCKING? It's a correctness bug in the changed code (crash of a previously-working command class). Severity: 🚨 BLOCKING per "merge would cause a bug".

Hmm — but wait. Is `cat` even reachable with binary files on mobile? Yes — users/models cat PNGs, tarballs. And AC6's own recipe downloads a tarball — `cat` of it isn't needed, but `tar -xzf` reads it. Still, `cat binary` is legitimate.

Also note: even a UTF-8 text cat now double-reads (seam probe + applet). Perf: IMPORTANT.

Next, let me look at other changed regions: memory_shell/paths.dart current state, builtin_tools_read.dart, builtin_tools_bash.dart context (timeoutArg usage), shell_jobs, agent_loop. Then check the env builtin in wasm_shell (`_envBuiltin`) — uses renderEnvListingWithSecretPresence on mobile too (saw in diff). 

Also check: `FA_SECRET_VARS` value in `_envBuiltin` on mobile — the roster rides `options.env`? In wasm_shell `_envBuiltin` merges `{...env, ...assignments}` where env is the stage env (which includes FA_SECRET_VARS via exec env). renderEnvListingWithSecretPresence hides FA_SECRET_VARS. Good.

But — `printenv FA_SECRET_VARS` on mobile: coreutils printenv applet reads env → prints names. Fine (names only).

Security check — `redact`: does the roster leak SECRET NAMES in logs? Names are like FA_GITHUB_TOKEN — presence of names in app.log? The roster env var is passed to WASI stages; the env values are visible in `rec.configs.single.env` (test logs). Not secret values. OK per threat model ("PRESENT/ABSENT leaks presence only").

One more security angle: `secretPresenceLine` renders `NAME: PRESENT` when a non-empty value is in env. Suppose a user sets a PLAIN env var named e.g. `PATH` — not rostered — renders `PATH=/bin`. Fine.

Now — an important behavioral check for `renderEnvListingWithSecretPresence`: the OLD behavior of `env` on the web shell printed ALL vars including secret values?? Pre-PR: `names.map((n) => '$n=${env[n]}')` — wait, the SecretsExecutionEnv injects secret VALUES into the exec env. So pre-PR, `env` in the sandbox PRINTED SECRET VALUES?! Hmm — no wait. Which env does the shell's env builtin see? The stage env = the exec env (with injected secret values). So pre-PR `env` would print `FA_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_...`! That was the leak AC4 fixes... The ticket says C4: "$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN empty on first authenticated call" and "redaction removes values, never the variable's existence signal". Hmm, but there's a jobLogRedactor / redaction layer. Anyway — this PR FIXES that leak for mobile/web shells. Good.

BUT: what about `echo $FA_GITHUB_TOKEN`? Still prints the value (by design, bash needs it). And `printenv FA_GITHUB_TOKEN` on mobile — printenv is a coreutils applet reading the WASI env → prints the VALUE. So secret values remain obtainable via printenv — pre-existing (bash expansion too). Fine, documented design ($NAME must work).

Desktop LocalShell: `env` builtin = real /usr/bin/env → prints `FA_SECRET_VARS=...` AND the actual secret values (pre-existing behavior — LocalShell env prints real env). Not changed here. The desktop surface isn't patched to render PRESENT/ABSENT — cross-sandbox REG inconsistency (ticket test plan explicitly says REG must behave identically or degrade with explicit note). On desktop, `env` will print values as before AND the roster var (names). The PR adds `FA_SECRET_VARS` to desktop env listings via LocalShell — meaning on DESKTOP, `env` now shows `FA_SECRET_VARS=FA_GITHUB_TOKEN ...` — a NEW env var visible to every child process and in every env dump. Benign (names only), but it changes desktop "byte-identical" REG goldens? The ticket non-goal says "No change to desktop CLI behavior beyond shared pure modules (guarded by REG goldens)". But SecretsExecutionEnv is shared — desktop CLI exec envs NOW carry FA_SECRET_VARS. That IS a desktop behavior change (env dumps in desktop bash now include the roster var; any test asserting exact env maps broke — they updated test/secrets/secrets_test.dart accordingly, which is core, so CI test-core should catch others... they did update). The REG golden claim "CLI/desktop unaffected paths byte-identical" is not quite true for env listings on desktop. Minor documentation/consistency gap. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? Now I have a fairly complete picture. Let me consolidate my findings and check a couple of remaining specifics:

BLOCKING — CI red (2 failures): Quality gate (dart analyze non-zero due to 2 NEW analyzer warnings at lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart:375 `if (timeoutArg != null ...` — unnecessary_null_comparison + dead_code, reproduced locally vs clean main) and Flutter CRAP ratchet (new/changed flutter_app functions exceed CRAP 30 vs baseline — SandboxBuiltins.curl grew, _catBuiltin/_catNeedsPointerSeam/WasiPythonNoiseFilter added).

2. BLOCKING — binary `cat` regression on mobile: `_catNeedsPointerSeam` probe calls `_readSandboxText(path)` → `file.readAsString()` which throws FileSystemException on non-UTF-8 content → escapes `exec()` as an uncaught exception (callers expect Result, not throws). Verified `readAsString` throws on binary. Line in diff: wasm_shell.dart `_catNeedsPointerSeam` (need the exact diff line number).

Also even for valid UTF-8 cats: double read (probe + applet) — inefficiency, and for binary it's a crash. Let me get the exact line numbers in the diff for the inline comments.

3. IMPORTANT — roster only covers granted names: `SecretsExecutionEnv.mergedExecEnv` registers `secrets.keys` (granted), so a name listed in the prompt but never granted renders NO line (absent signal missing) — the exact C4 evidence scenario ("$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN empty on first authenticated call" — token not yet granted). The comment in execution_env.dart claims "the prompt's name list doubles as the sandbox env presence roster" but the wiring doesn't deliver the never-granted case.

4. IMPORTANT — `_catBuiltin` double-read for every pointer-seam cat (probe + applet full read) — performance on large files; plus probe reads full file just to check first bytes.

Actually the crash and double-read are the same root cause; I'll merge: the seam probe should read only a bounded prefix via readAsBytes + check, not readAsString.

5. IMPORTANT — the `timeoutArg != null` dead code also means the sandbox silently ignores the timeout arg rather than the intended TODO resolution; the analyzer warning is the gate break; the dead-code semantics: timeout never applied to the WASI pipeline run. That's actually a functional gap: `timeout 30 curl ...` in the sandbox ignores the 30 (the pipeline has its own exec timeout via options.timeout though). The PR description mentions "timeout arg parsing" as a driver. Semantics: parsed but unused. Worth an IMPORTANT (or fold into the blocking analyzer one). 6. IMPORTANT — `bridgeHostOfAuthority` doesn't strip IPv6 brackets: `curl http://[::1]:8080/` → host `[::1]` never matches `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` → treated as remote → full failure plumbing for a loopback request. Minor; SUGGESTION probably. Hmm — severity: it's an edge case; SUGGESTION.

7. IMPORTANT — AC6 gap: the "codeload blocked → tarball recipe" fix is documentation + unit-test simulation only; no actual bridge/redirect behavior change (followRedirects=false remains on the python bridge — that's the python_http_bridge, which is for pip; the curl builtin follows redirects itself). The simulator leg is deferred (PR admits). Also `curl -L codeload` → 302 → objects.githubusercontent.com is followed by the builtin's own redirect loop (MAX_REDIRECTS). So AC6's mechanics were already fine for the curl builtin; the fix is prompt documentation. The E2E on a real device is unverifiable → note as accepted-gap in general comment (ticket says REG deferral needs explicit note — the PR does note it).

8. SUGGESTION — `renderEnvListingWithSecretPresence` on desktop: desktop `env` (real /usr/bin/env) now also shows `FA_SECRET_VARS=...` names in every env dump — cross-surface inconsistency (mobile/web render PRESENT/ABSENT; desktop prints values like before + roster names). Not a leak of values beyond pre-existing behavior; note.

Wait — actually on desktop, does SecretsExecutionEnv wrap LocalShell? Yes — exec envs are shared; LocalShell.exec gets options.env merged over Platform.environment → FA_SECRET_VARS present in real child env, so `/usr/bin/env` prints it. Pre-existing desktop secrets behavior unchanged otherwise. SUGGESTION.

9. Test-gap SUGGESTION: no unit test for `_catNeedsPointerSeam` binary path (the crash I found is untested); flutter tests cover pointer seam with text content only.

10. `WasiPythonNoiseFilter` — latin1 wrapper for gzip/bzip2 appends newlines and passes through "K\nK\n" artifact lines on trailing NULs; acceptable, documented in tests. OK.

2. BLOCKING — binary `cat` regression on mobile: `_catNeedsPointerSeam` probe calls `_readSandboxText(path)` → `file.readAsString()` which throws FileSystemException on non-UTF-8 content → escapes `exec()` as an uncaught exception (callers expect Result, not throws). Verified `readAsString` throws on binary. Line in diff: wasm_shell.dart `_catNeedsPointerSeam` (need the exact diff line number).

Also even for valid UTF-8 cats: double read (probe + applet) — inefficiency, and for binary it's a crash. Let me get the exact line numbers in the diff for the inline comments.

3. IMPORTANT — roster only covers granted names: `SecretsExecutionEnv.mergedExecEnv` registers `secrets.keys` (granted), so a name listed in the prompt but never granted renders NO line (absent signal missing) — the exact C4 evidence scenario ("$FA_GITHUB_TOKEN empty on first authenticated call" — token not yet granted). The comment in execution_env.dart claims "the prompt's name list doubles as the sandbox env presence roster" but the wiring doesn't deliver the never-granted case.

4. IMPORTANT — `_catBuiltin` double-read for every pointer-seam cat (probe + applet full read) — performance on large files; plus probe reads full file just to check first bytes.

Actually the crash and double-read are the same root cause; I'll merge: the seam probe should read only a bounded prefix via readAsBytes + check, not readAsString.

IMPORTANT — the `timeoutArg != null` dead code also means the sandbox silently ignores the timeout arg rather than the intended TODO resolution; the analyzer warning is the gate break; the dead-code semantics: timeout never applied to the WASI pipeline run. 7. IMPORTANT — AC6 gap: the "codeload blocked → tarball recipe" fix is documentation + unit-test simulation only; no actual bridge/redirect behavior change (followRedirects=false remains on the python bridge — that's the python_http_bridge, which is for pip; the curl builtin follows redirects itself). The simulator leg is deferred (PR admits). Also `curl -L codeload` → 302 → objects.githubusercontent.com is followed by the builtin's own redirect loop (MAX_REDIRECTS). So AC6's mechanics were already fine for the curl builtin; the fix is prompt documentation. The E2E on a real device is unverifiable → note as accepted-gap in general comment (ticket says REG deferral needs explicit note — the PR does note it).

8. SUGGESTION — `renderEnvListingWithSecretPresence` on desktop: desktop `env` (real /usr/bin/env) now also shows `FA_SECRET_VARS=...` names in every env dump — cross-surface inconsistency (mobile/web render PRESENT/ABSENT; desktop prints values like before + roster names). Pre-existing desktop secrets behavior unchanged otherwise. SUGGESTION.

9. Test-gap SUGGESTION: no unit test for `_catNeedsPointerSeam` binary path (the crash I found is untested); flutter tests cover pointer seam with text content only.

10. `WasiPythonNoiseFilter` — latin1 wrapper for gzip/bzip2 appends newlines and passes through "K\nK\n" artifact lines on trailing NULs; acceptable, documented in tests. OK.
